sentences.zh: 豫章文獻王嶷字宣儼，太祖第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang, Ni, courtesy name Xuan Yan, was the Grand Ancestor's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang, Xiao Ni, courtesy name Xuan Yan, was the second son of Xiao Daocheng, the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 寬仁弘雅，有大成之量，太祖特鍾愛焉。

translations.literal: Generous, humane, broad and refined, he had the measure of great completion; the Grand Ancestor loved him especially.
translations.idiomatic: He was magnanimous, humane, and cultivated, with the breadth to bring things to completion; Xiao Daocheng doted on him above the rest.

sentences.zh: 起家為太學博士、長城令，入為尚書左民郎、錢唐令。

translations.literal: He began his career as erudite of the Imperial University and magistrate of Changcheng, then entered office as gentleman of the left bureau for the people in the Secretariat and magistrate of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: He began as erudite of the Imperial University and magistrate of Changcheng, then entered the capital as gentleman of the left bureau for the people and magistrate of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 太祖破薛索兒，改封西陽，以先爵賜為晉壽縣侯。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor defeated Xue Suo'er, his fief was changed to Xiyang and his former noble title was granted as Marquis of Jinshou county.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Daocheng defeated Xue Suo'er, Ni's fief was changed to Xiyang and his former title was given as Marquis of Jinshou county.

sentences.zh: 除通直散騎侍郎，以偏憂去官。

translations.literal: He was appointed attendant cavalier in regular attendance but left office for partial mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was named attendant cavalier in regular attendance but left office for partial mourning.

sentences.zh: 桂陽之役，太祖出頓新亭壘，板嶷為寧朔將軍，領兵衞從。

translations.literal: In the Guiyang campaign the Grand Ancestor went out to encamp at Xinting fortress and commissioned Ni as General Who Pacifies the North, commanding troops as bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Liu Zixun of Guiyang, Xiao Daocheng went out to hold Xinting fortress and commissioned Ni as General Who Pacifies the North to command the guard.

sentences.zh: 休範率士卒攻壘南，嶷執白虎幡督戰，屢摧卻之。

translations.literal: Xiufan led soldiers to attack the south of the fortress; Ni took the White Tiger banner to direct battle and repeatedly beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiufan led troops against the south face of the fortress; Ni took the White Tiger banner to direct the fight and drove them back again and again.

sentences.zh: 事寧，遷中書郎。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was transferred to gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis was over he was transferred to gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋為安遠護軍、武陵內史。

translations.literal: Soon after he became Protector of the Army for Pacifying the Distance and interior secretary of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became protector of the army for pacifying the distance and interior secretary of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 時沈攸之責賧，伐荊州界內諸蠻，遂

translations.literal: At that time Shen Youzhi demanded tribute and attacked the various barbarians within Jing province's borders, and then
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shen Youzhi was exacting tribute and attacking the barbarian peoples within Jing province's borders, and then

translations.literal: Collation: the received text reads fan "rebel"; ji "reach" is adopted below.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: received fan, emended to ji.

sentences.zh: 〔及〕五溪，禁斷魚鹽。

translations.literal: Reached the Five Streams and banned trade in fish and salt.
translations.idiomatic: Reached the Five Streams and banned trade in fish and salt.

sentences.zh: 羣蠻怒，酉溪蠻王田頭擬殺攸之使，攸之責賧千萬，頭擬輸五百萬，發氣死。

translations.literal: The various barbarians were enraged. Tian Touni, king of the Youxi barbarians, was about to kill Shen Youzhi's envoy; Shen Youzhi demanded ten million in tribute; Touni was to deliver five million but died of rage.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were enraged. Tian Touni, king of the Youxi Miao, was about to kill Shen Youzhi's envoy; Youzhi demanded ten million in tribute; Touni was to pay five million but died of fury.

sentences.zh: 其弟婁侯篡立，頭擬子田都走入獠中，於是蠻部大亂，抄掠平民，至郡城下。

translations.literal: His brother Louhou usurped the throne; Touni's son Tiandu fled into the Liao lands. Then the barbarian departments fell into great disorder, raiding common people as far as the commandery city.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Louhou seized power; Touni's son Tiandu fled among the Liao. The tribal departments fell into chaos and raided the countryside as far as the commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 〔嶷〕遣隊主張莫兒率將吏擊破之。

translations.literal: 〔Ni〕sent squad commander Zhang Mo'er to lead officers and troops to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Ni sent squad commander Zhang Mo'er with officers and soldiers to break them.

sentences.zh: 田都自獠中請立，而婁侯懼，亦歸附。

translations.literal: Tiandu from among the Liao asked to be installed; Louhou in fear also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tiandu came out of the Liao to ask to succeed; Louhou, in fear, submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 嶷誅婁侯於郡獄，命田都繼其父，蠻眾乃安。

translations.literal: Ni executed Louhou in the commandery prison, ordered Tiandu to succeed his father, and the barbarian masses were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ni executed Louhou in the commandery prison, installed Tiandu in his father's place, and the tribes were quieted.

sentences.zh: 入為宋從帝車騎諮議參軍、府掾，轉驃騎，仍遷從事中郎。

translations.literal: He entered office as staff counselor to the chariots and cavalry of Emperor Shun of Song and staff aide, transferred to the Rapid Cavalry staff, and was then promoted attending gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as staff counselor on Emperor Shun of Song's chariots-and-cavalry staff and as a headquarters aide, moved to the Rapid Cavalry staff, and was then promoted attending gentleman.

sentences.zh: 詣司徒袁粲，粲謂人曰：「後來佳器也。」

translations.literal: He called on Minister of Works Yuan Can; Can said to someone, 「A vessel of future excellence.」
translations.idiomatic: He called on the Minister of Works Yuan Can; Can told someone, 「Here is a vessel of future excellence.」

sentences.zh: 太祖在領軍府，嶷居

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor was at the Director General's office, Ni lodged at the
translations.idiomatic: While Xiao Daocheng held the Director General's post, Ni lived at the

translations.literal: Collation: the received text reads qing "clear"; qing "azure" is adopted below.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: received qing (clear), emended to qing (azure).

sentences.zh: 〔青〕溪宅。

translations.literal: 〔qing〕stream residence.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxi residence.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王夜中微行，欲掩襲宅內，嶷〔令〕左右儛刀戟於中庭，蒼梧從墻閒窺見，以為有備，乃去。

translations.literal: Emperor Houfei of Liu Song made a secret night expedition intending a surprise attack on the residence; Ni 〔ordered〕 his attendants to brandish blades and halberds in the central courtyard. Houfei peered through a gap in the wall, thought preparations had been made, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Houfei of Liu Song went out by night in secret, intending a surprise on the house; Ni had his attendants brandish blades and halberds in the courtyard. Houfei peered through a gap in the wall, saw that the place was ready, and left.

sentences.zh: 太祖帶南兖州，鎮軍府長史蕭順之在鎮，憂危既切，期渡江北起兵。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor held southern Yan province; Chief Clerk Xiao Shunzhi of the Pacifying Army headquarters was at the garrison. Peril was pressing and they planned to cross the Yangtze north to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng held southern Yan province; Xiao Shunzhi, chief clerk on the pacifying army staff, was at the garrison. Danger pressed close, and they set a date to cross the Yangtze north and raise troops.

sentences.zh: 嶷諫曰：「主上狂凶，人下不自保，單行道路，易以立功。

translations.literal: Ni remonstrated, saying, 「The sovereign is mad and cruel; those below cannot keep themselves safe. To go alone on the road is the easy way to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ni remonstrated: 「The sovereign is mad and cruel; no one beneath him is safe. To go alone on the road is the easy way to merit.

sentences.zh: 外州起兵，鮮有克勝。

translations.literal: To raise troops in an outer province—few ever win.
translations.idiomatic: To raise troops from an outer province—few ever win.

sentences.zh: 物情疑惑，必先人受禍。

translations.literal: Men's hearts are doubtful; someone else will suffer disaster first.
translations.idiomatic: Men's hearts will be doubtful; disaster will strike another first.

sentences.zh: 今於此立計，萬不可失。

translations.literal: To set a plan here now is a chance that must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: To lay a plan here now is a chance that must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 」蒼梧王殞，太祖報嶷曰：「大事已判，汝明可早入。

translations.literal: 」When Houfei died, the Grand Ancestor sent word to Ni: 「The great affair is decided—you, Ming, may enter early.
translations.idiomatic: 」When Houfei died, Xiao Daocheng sent word to Ni: 「The great affair is decided—you, Ming, may enter early.

sentences.zh: 」從帝即位，轉侍中，總宮內直衞。

translations.literal: 」When Shun of Song took the throne, Ni was transferred to palace attendant and oversaw the inner palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: 」When Emperor Shun of Song took the throne, Ni was made palace attendant and put in charge of the inner palace guard.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之之難，太祖入朝堂，嶷出鎮東府，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: In Shen Youzhi's crisis the Grand Ancestor entered the court hall; Ni went out to garrison the Eastern Palace and was given the additional title general of the champions.
translations.idiomatic: During Shen Youzhi's revolt Xiao Daocheng entered the court hall while Ni went out to hold the Eastern Palace and was given the additional title general of the champions.

sentences.zh: 袁粲舉兵夕，丹陽丞王遜告變，先至東府，嶷遣帳內軍主戴元孫二千人隨薛道淵等俱至石頭，焚門之功，元孫預焉。

translations.literal: On the evening Yuan Can raised troops, Assistant Administrator of Danyang Wang Xun reported the mutiny and reached the Eastern Palace first. Ni sent Personal Guard Commander Dai Yuansun with two thousand men to follow Xue Daoyuan and the rest to Stone City; in burning the gates Yuansun took part.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening Yuan Can rose, Wang Xun, assistant administrator of Danyang, reported the mutiny and reached the Eastern Palace first. Ni sent his personal guard commander Dai Yuansun with two thousand men after Xue Daoyuan and the rest to Stone City; Yuansun shared in burning the gates.

sentences.zh: 先是王蘊薦部曲六十人助為城防，實以為內應也。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Yun had recommended sixty retainers to help with city defense—they were in fact to serve as inside contacts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Yun had recommended sixty retainers to help hold the city—they were meant as inside contacts.

sentences.zh: 嶷知蘊懷貳，不給其仗，散處外省。

translations.literal: Ni knew Yun harbored divided loyalty, gave them no weapons, and scattered them in outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: Ni knew Yun was double-minded, gave them no arms, and scattered them in outer offices.

sentences.zh: 及難作搜檢，皆已亡去。

translations.literal: When the crisis broke and searches were made, all had already fled.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble broke out and searches were made, all had already fled.

sentences.zh: 遷中領軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to central commander of the guards and given the additional post attendant cavalier at large.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to central commander of the guards with the additional post of attendant cavalier at large.

sentences.zh: 上流平後，世祖自尋陽還，嶷出為使持節、都督江州豫州之新蔡晉熙二郡軍事、左將軍、江州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: After the upper reaches were pacified, Shizu returned from Xunyang. Ni was sent out as bearer of the staff, superintendent of military affairs for Xin Cai and Jinxi of Jiang and Yu provinces, General of the Left, and inspector of Jiang—but kept his cavalier appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After the upper Yangtze was pacified, Shizu returned from Xunyang. Ni was sent out as bearer of the staff, superintendent of Xin Cai and Jinxi in Jiang and Yu, General of the Left, and inspector of Jiang, with his cavalier post unchanged.

sentences.zh: 給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was granted one suite of guard music.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one suite of guard music.

sentences.zh: 以定策功，改封永安縣公，千五百戶。

translations.literal: For service in settling the succession he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yong'an county, fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For helping settle the succession he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Yong'an county, fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 仍徙都督荊湘雍益梁寧南北秦八州諸軍事、鎮西將軍、荊州刺史，持節、常侍如故。

translations.literal: He was then transferred as superintendent of military affairs over eight provinces—Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, North Qin, and South Qin—General Who Pacifies the West, and inspector of Jing, bearer of the staff and cavalier as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made superintendent of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, North Qin, and South Qin, General Who Pacifies the West, and inspector of Jing, with staff and cavalier post as before.

sentences.zh: 時太祖輔政，〔嶷〕務在省約，停府州儀迎物。

translations.literal: While the Grand Ancestor assisted the government, 〔Ni〕devoted himself to frugality, suspending the welcoming paraphernalia of headquarters and province.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiao Daocheng assisted the government, Ni devoted himself to economy, halting the welcoming displays of headquarters and province.

sentences.zh: 初，沈攸之欲聚眾，開民相告，士庶坐執役者甚眾。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shen Youzhi wished to gather troops, he encouraged people to inform on one another; gentry and commoners held for corvée labor were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shen Youzhi tried to gather troops, he set people informing on one another; gentry and commoners pressed into corvée were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 嶷至鎮，一日遣三千餘人。

translations.literal: When Ni reached his post, in a single day he released more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Ni reached his post, in a single day he released more than three thousand.

sentences.zh: 見囚五歲刑以下不連臺者，皆原遣。

translations.literal: Prisoners under five years' punishment not connected with the central administration—all were pardoned and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners sentenced to five years or less who were not tied to central cases were all pardoned and sent home.

sentences.zh: 以市稅重濫，更定㮧格，以稅還民。

translations.literal: Because market taxes were heavy and excessive, he set new tax schedules and returned the proceeds to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Because market levies were heavy and abusive, he set new tax brackets and returned the revenue to the people.

sentences.zh: 禁諸市調及苗籍。

translations.literal: He forbade all market levies and household registration taxes at the markets.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade market surcharges and household registration fees in the markets.

sentences.zh: 二千石官長不得與人為

translations.literal: Officials of two-thousand-shi rank must not trade with people in the
translations.idiomatic: Officials of two-thousand-shi rank were forbidden to trade with people in the

translations.literal: Collation: the received text reads gong "duke"; shi "market" is adopted below.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: received gong, emended to shi.

translations.literal: Market,
translations.idiomatic: Market,

translations.literal: Collation: the received text reads yi "fitting"; zhu "various" is adopted below.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: received yi, emended to zhu.

sentences.zh: 〔諸〕曹吏聽分番假。

translations.literal: Clerks in the various bureaus were permitted rotating leave by shift.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks in the various bureaus were allowed leave in rotating shifts.

sentences.zh: 百姓甚悅。

translations.literal: The common people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The people were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 禪讓之閒，世祖欲速定大業，嶷依違其事，默無所言。

translations.literal: During the interval of the abdication, Emperor Wu wished to settle the great enterprise quickly; Ni wavered over the affair and said nothing aloud.
translations.idiomatic: In the days of the abdication, Emperor Wu wanted the succession fixed at once; Xiao Ni hung back and kept silent.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，太祖即位，赦詔未至，嶷先下令蠲除

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, when the Grand Ancestor took the throne, the amnesty edict had not yet arrived, yet Ni first ordered cancellation of
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year 1, when the Grand Ancestor took the throne, the amnesty edict had not yet come down, yet Ni first ordered remission of

translations.literal: (state)
translations.idiomatic: (emended: department)

sentences.zh: 〔部〕內昇明二年以前逋負。

translations.literal: within his jurisdiction all arrears from before the second year of Shengming.
translations.idiomatic: all arrears within his jurisdiction dating from before Shengming year 2.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、尚書令、都督揚南徐二州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace attendant, director of the masters of writing, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Yang and South Xu provinces, grand general of cavalry, bearer of the staff with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Yang province, his staff of authority unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was made palace attendant and director of the masters of writing, commander-in-chief in Yang and South Xu, grand general of cavalry, bearer of the staff equal to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Yang, with his commission unchanged.

sentences.zh: 封豫章郡王，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as prince of Yuzhang commandery with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as prince of Yuzhang with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 僕射王儉牋曰：「舊楚蕭條，仍歲多故，荒民散亡，寔須緝理。

translations.literal: Vice director Wang Jian wrote in a memorial: 「The old lands of Chu are desolate; year after year brings new troubles; scattered refugees truly need binding up in order.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wang Jian wrote: 「The old Chu lands lie waste; year on year brings fresh trouble; refugees scattered abroad must be gathered and set in order.

sentences.zh: 公臨莅甫爾，英風惟穆，江、漢來蘇，八州慕義。

translations.literal: Your Grace has only just arrived, yet noble bearing spreads calm; along the Yangzi and Han the people revive; eight provinces look up in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Your Grace has only just taken office, yet your bearing already brings calm; along the Yangzi and Han the people breathe again; eight provinces turn to you in trust.

sentences.zh: 自庾亮以來，荊楚無復如此美政。

translations.literal: Since Yu Liang, Jing and Chu have known no governance so fine.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yu Liang, Jing and Chu have not seen rule like this.

sentences.zh: 古人朞月有成，而公旬日致治，豈不休哉！」

translations.literal: The ancients expected a full month for results, yet Your Grace brought order in ten days—how could it not be splendid!」
translations.idiomatic: The ancients looked for a month's work; Your Grace brought order in ten days—what could be finer?」

sentences.zh: 會北虜動，上思為經略。

translations.literal: Just then the northern enemy stirred, and the throne turned to strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the northerners moved, and the court turned to strategy.

sentences.zh: 乃詔曰：「神牧總司王畿，誠為治要；

translations.literal: An edict said: 「The sacred pasture that oversees the royal domains is truly the hinge of rule;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: 「The sacred shepherd who holds the royal domain is the true pivot of government;

sentences.zh: 荊楚領馭遐遠，任寄弘隆。

translations.literal: Jing-Chu holds sway over the far marches, and the commission is weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Chu govern the distant marches, and the charge laid upon them is great.

sentences.zh: 自頃公私凋盡，綏撫之宜，尤重恒日。

translations.literal: Of late public and private stores are drained; soothing the land must weigh heavy every day.」
translations.idiomatic: Lately public and private means are spent; to soothe the land must be the daily burden.」

sentences.zh: 」復以為都督荊湘雍益梁寧南北秦八州諸軍事、南蠻校尉、荊湘二州刺史，持節、侍中、將軍、開府如故。

translations.literal: He was again made commander-in-chief of military affairs in Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, and North and South Qin, colonel over the southern barbarians, and inspector of Jing and Xiang provinces; his staff, palace attendant rank, generalship, and open office were as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made commander-in-chief over Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Liang, Ning, and North and South Qin, colonel over the southern barbarians, and inspector of Jing and Xiang; his staff, palace attendant rank, generalship, and open office stood as before.

sentences.zh: 晉宋之際，刺史多不領南蠻，別以重人居之，至是有二府二州。

translations.literal: Between Jin and Song, inspectors often did not personally hold the southern barbarians post; a weighty man was set apart for it—now there were two staffs and two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Between Jin and Song, inspectors often did not themselves hold the southern barbarians command; a man of weight was set apart for it—now there were two staffs and two provinces.

sentences.zh: 荊州資費歲錢三千萬，布萬匹，米六萬斛，又以江、湘二州米十萬斛給鎮府，湘州資費歲七百萬，布三千匹，米五萬斛，南蠻資費歲三百萬，布萬匹，綿千斤，絹三百匹，米千斛，近代莫比也。

translations.literal: Jing province's yearly allowance was thirty million cash, ten thousand bolts of cloth, and sixty thousand hu of grain; another hundred thousand hu from Jiang and Xiang provinces supplied the headquarters. Xiang's yearly allowance was seven million cash, three thousand bolts of cloth, and fifty thousand hu of grain; the southern barbarians command's yearly allowance was three million cash, ten thousand bolts of cloth, a thousand jin of floss, three hundred bolts of silk, and a thousand hu of grain—in recent times nothing matched it.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's yearly provision was thirty million cash, ten thousand bolts of cloth, and sixty thousand hu of grain; another hundred thousand hu from Jiang and Xiang fed the headquarters. Xiang drew seven million cash, three thousand bolts, and fifty thousand hu a year; the southern barbarians command drew three million cash, ten thousand bolts, a thousand jin of floss, three hundred bolts of silk, and a thousand hu of grain—nothing in recent memory compared.

sentences.zh: 尋給油絡俠望車。

translations.literal: Soon he was given an oil-lacquered carriage with outrider guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was granted an oil-lacquered carriage with outrider escort.

sentences.zh: 二年春，虜寇司、豫二州，嶷表遣南蠻司馬崔慧景北討，又分遣中兵參軍蕭惠朗援司州，屯西關。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year, the enemy raided Si and Yu provinces; Ni memorialized to send the southern barbarians staff officer Cui Huijing north to strike, and separately sent Central Army aide Xiao Huilang to aid Si province, encamped at West Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 2 the enemy raided Si and Yu; Ni memorialized to send the southern barbarians staff officer Cui Huijing north, and detached Central Army aide Xiao Huilang to reinforce Si, encamped at West Pass.

sentences.zh: 虜軍濟淮攻壽春，分騎當出隨、鄧，眾以為憂，嶷曰：「虜入春夏，非動眾時，令豫、司彊守遏其津要，彼見堅嚴，自當潰散，必不敢越二鎮而南也。

translations.literal: The enemy crossed the Huai to attack Shouchun; cavalry were expected to come out through Sui and Deng—many were anxious. Ni said: 「When barbarians enter in spring and summer, it is not the season for mass campaigns. Order Yu and Si to hold the crossings in strength; once they see firm walls, they will break of themselves—they will never dare march south past those two commands.」
translations.idiomatic: The enemy crossed the Huai against Shouchun; horsemen were expected through Sui and Deng, and many were afraid. Ni said: 「In spring and summer the northerners do not move in force. Let Yu and Si hold the crossings hard; when they see walls that will not yield, they will scatter—they will not dare slip south past those two commands.」

sentences.zh: 」是時纂嚴，嶷以荊州隣接蠻、蜑，慮其生心，令鎮內皆緩服。

translations.literal: At that time mobilization was ordered; Ni, because Jing bordered the Man and Dan peoples, feared they would stir, and had everyone within the command wear plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: Mobilization was ordered; Jing lay against Man and Dan country, and Ni, fearing hearts there would turn, had the whole command go in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 既而虜竟不出樊、鄧，於壽春敗走。

translations.literal: In the end the enemy never came out through Fan and Deng; they were defeated fleeing from Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the enemy never came through Fan and Deng; they were beaten and fled from Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 尋給班劍二十人。

translations.literal: Soon he was given twenty ceremonial swords as escort.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was granted twenty ceremonial swords as escort.

sentences.zh: 其夏，於南蠻園東南開館立學，上表言狀。

translations.literal: That summer, southeast of the Southern Barbarians Garden he opened a lodge and founded a school, memorializing the fact.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he opened a lodge and school southeast of the Southern Barbarians Garden and memorialized the plan.

sentences.zh: 置生四十人，取舊族父祖位正佐臺郎，年二十五以下十五以上補之，置儒林參軍一人，文學祭酒一人，勸學從事二人，行釋菜禮。

translations.literal: Forty students were enrolled, drawn from old families whose fathers and grandfathers had held the rank of full or assistant Masters of Writing at court, aged fifteen to twenty-five; one aide for the Confucian Forest, one libationer of letters, and two aides for encouraging study were appointed, and the ceremony of offering vegetables was performed.
translations.idiomatic: Forty students were taken from old houses whose fathers and grandfathers had been full or assistant masters of writing at court, between fifteen and twenty-five; one Confucian Forest aide, one libationer of letters, and two aides for encouraging study were named, and the vegetable offering rite was held.

sentences.zh: 以糓過賤，聽民以米當口錢，優評斛一百。

translations.literal: Because grain was too cheap, the people were allowed to pay their poll tax in rice at a favorable reckoning of a hundred per hu.
translations.idiomatic: Grain had grown too cheap; the people were allowed to pay poll tax in rice at a favorable rate of a hundred per hu.

sentences.zh: 義陽劫帥張羣亡命積年，鼓行為賊，義陽、武陵、天門、南平四郡界，被其殘破。

translations.literal: Zhang Qun, a bandit chieftain of Yiyang, had been an outlaw for years, marching in revolt; the bounds of Yiyang, Wuling, Tianmen, and Nanping commands were ravaged by him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qun, a robber chief of Yiyang, had been a fugitive for years, marching as a rebel; Yiyang, Wuling, Tianmen, and Nanping were laid waste along their borders.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之連討不能禽，乃首用之。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi pursued him repeatedly without capture, and finally enlisted him at the head of his force.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi hunted him again and again without taking him, and in the end put him at the head of his ranks.

sentences.zh: 攸之起事，羣從下郢，於路先叛，結寨於三溪，依據深險。

translations.literal: When Youzhi rose in rebellion, Qun marched down from Xia, but rebelled on the road first, built a stockade at Three Streams, and held deep defiles.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi rose, Qun came down from Xia, turned rebel on the road, and walled himself at Three Streams in steep country.

sentences.zh: 嶷遣中兵參軍虞欣祖為義陽太守，使降意誘納之，厚為禮遺，於坐斬首，其黨數百人皆散，四郡獲安。

translations.literal: Ni sent Central Army aide Yu Xizu as administrator of Yiyang to feign surrender and lure Qun in; with rich gifts at the feast he beheaded him on the spot; several hundred followers scattered, and the four commands knew peace.
translations.idiomatic: Ni sent Central Army aide Yu Xizu as administrator of Yiyang to feign surrender and draw Qun in; at the feast, with gifts heaped around him, Qun was beheaded where he sat; several hundred of his band scattered, and the four commands were quiet.

sentences.zh: 入為都督揚南徐二州諸軍事、中書監、司空、揚州刺史，持節、侍中如故。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as commander of Yang and South Xu, palace library inspector, minister of works, and inspector of Yang; his staff and palace attendant rank were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as commander of Yang and South Xu, palace library inspector, minister of works, and inspector of Yang; his staff and palace attendant rank stood as before.

sentences.zh: 加兵置佐。

translations.literal: Military aides were added to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Military aides were added to his staff.

sentences.zh: 以前軍臨川王映府文武配司空府。

translations.literal: The civil and military officers of the former army of Prince Ying of Linchuan were assigned to the ministry of works staff.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military staff of Prince Ying of Linchuan's former army were assigned to the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 嶷以將還都，脩治廨宇及路陌，東歸部曲不得齎府州物出城。

translations.literal: As Ni was about to return to the capital, he had government halls and roads repaired; eastern units returning were forbidden to carry prefectural or commandery goods out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: As Ni prepared to return to the capital, he had government halls and roads put in order; eastern units going home were forbidden to carry prefectural or commandery goods out of the walls.

sentences.zh: 發江津，士女觀送數千人，皆垂泣。

translations.literal: Setting out from Jiangjin, several thousand men and women lined the road to see him off, all in tears.
translations.idiomatic: He set out from Jiangjin; several thousand men and women watched him go, weeping.

sentences.zh: 嶷發江陵感疾，至京師未瘳，上深憂慮，為之大赦，三年六月壬子赦令是也。

translations.literal: Ni fell ill setting out from Jiangling; he had not recovered when he reached the capital; the throne was deeply anxious and proclaimed a general amnesty on his account—the amnesty of renzi in the sixth month of year 3.
translations.idiomatic: Ni fell ill leaving Jiangling and had not mended by the time he reached the capital; the throne was deeply troubled and proclaimed a general amnesty for his sake—the renzi amnesty of the sixth month of year 3.

sentences.zh: 疾愈，上幸東府設金石樂，敕得乘輿至宮六門。

translations.literal: When he recovered, the emperor visited his Eastern Residence with bronze and stone music, and by edict permitted the imperial carriage to approach as far as the six gates of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When he was well again, the emperor came to his Eastern Residence with bronze and stone music and decreed that the imperial carriage might advance to the six palace gates.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，嶷哀號，眼耳皆出血。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor died, Ni wailed in grief until blood flowed from his eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor died, Ni wailed until blood ran from his eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，進位太尉，置兵佐，解侍中，增班劍為三十人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Ni was advanced to grand commandant, given military aides, relieved of palace attendant rank, and his ceremonial swords increased to thirty.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu acceded, Ni was advanced to grand commandant, given military aides, relieved of palace attendant, and his ceremonial swords raised to thirty.

translations.idiomatic: Jianyuan

translations.literal: During the era, Emperor Wu lost favor on some matter; the Grand Ancestor had had thoughts of replacing the heir apparent, but Ni served Emperor Wu with reverent courtesy to the full and never once showed a cross expression on his face, and so Emperor Wu's brotherly love was likewise deep.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianyuan years Emperor Wu once lost favor over an affair; the Grand Ancestor had thought of setting another heir in his place, but Ni served Emperor Wu with full reverent courtesy and never once let his face show defiance, and so the emperor's brotherly love ran deep as well.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，領太子太傅，解中書監，餘如故。

translations.literal: In Yongming year 1 he was made grand tutor of the heir apparent, relieved of palace library inspector, and otherwise unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 1 he was made grand tutor of the heir apparent, relieved of palace library inspector, and otherwise unchanged.

sentences.zh: 手啟上曰：「陛下以叡孝纂業，萬㝢惟新，諸弟有序，臣屢荷隆愛，叨授台首，不敢固辭，俛仰祗寵，心魂如失。

translations.literal: He wrote personally to the throne: 「Your Majesty has taken up the inheritance through sagely filial piety; the realm is anew; the imperial brothers are in order; I have again and again received towering favor and been honored with the head of the Secretariat—I dared not cling to refusal; bowing to your grace, my heart and soul seem lost.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to the throne in his own hand: 「Your Majesty has taken the inheritance through wise filial piety; the realm is made new; the imperial brothers stand in their ranks; I have again and again been heaped with favor and set at the head of the Secretariat—I did not dare hold out in refusal; bowing to your grace, heart and soul feel adrift.

sentences.zh: 負重量力，古今同規。

translations.literal: Bearing weight beyond one's strength is the same measure in every age.
translations.idiomatic: To bear more than one's strength allows is the same rule in every age.

sentences.zh: 臣窮生如浮，質操空素，任居鼎右，已移氣序，自頃以來，宿疾稍纏，心慮恍惚，表於容狀，視此根候，常恐命不勝恩。

translations.literal: My life is adrift as foam on water, my substance and conduct mere emptiness; placed at the right hand of the tripod, the seasons have already turned. Lately old illness has wound tighter; thoughts grow dim, plain on my face. By these signs I often fear my allotted span cannot bear so much grace.
translations.idiomatic: My life drifts like foam; substance and conduct are hollow; I sit at the right hand of the tripod and the seasons have already shifted. Lately old illness winds tighter; the mind grows dim and shows on the face. By these signs I often fear my span cannot carry so much grace.

sentences.zh: 加以星緯屢見災祥，雖脩短有恒，能不耿介。

translations.literal: Coupled with omens and constellations showing disaster again and again—though lifespan has its measure, who could remain unmoved?
translations.idiomatic: Stars and omens have shown disaster again and again; though life has its term, who could stand unmoved?

sentences.zh: 比心欲從俗，啟解今職，但厝辭為鄙，或貽物誚，所以息意緘嘿，一委時運，而可復加寵榮，增其顛墜。

translations.literal: Measuring by my heart, I would follow custom and beg release from my present post; but ill-chosen words would be vulgar, or invite the world's scorn—so I quiet my will and hold silence, leaving all to fate; yet how can favor and glory be piled on again and deepen my fall?
translations.idiomatic: By my heart I would follow custom and ask release from this office; but clumsy words would be base, or draw the world's mockery—so I quiet my will and keep silent, leaving all to fate; yet how can favor and glory be heaped on again and hasten my fall?

sentences.zh: 且儲傅之重，實非恒選，遂使太子見臣必束帶，宮臣皆再拜，二三之宜，何以當此。

translations.literal: Moreover, the weight of tutor to the heir is no ordinary appointment; it makes the crown prince gird himself when he sees me and palace officers all perform double bows—how can someone of second or third rank bear such things?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, tutor to the heir is no ordinary post: the crown prince girds himself when he sees me, palace officers all double-bow—how should a man of second or third rank bear it?

sentences.zh: 陛下同生十餘，今唯臣而已，友于之愛，豈當獨臣鍾其隆遇。

translations.literal: Your Majesty had more than ten born of one father; now I alone remain. Brotherly love—should I alone be singled out for such lavish favor?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty had more than ten brothers by one father; now I alone remain. Should brotherly love fall on me alone with such lavish favor?

sentences.zh: 別奉啟事，仰祈恩照。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial I beg your gracious attention.
translations.idiomatic: In a separate memorial I beg your gracious attention.

sentences.zh: 臣近亦侍言太子，告意子良，具因王儉申啟，未知粗上聞未？

translations.literal: Recently I also attended upon the crown prince and conveyed my mind to Ziliang, fully reported through Wang Jian—whether this has reached Your Majesty in rough outline, I do not know.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately attended the crown prince as well, spoken my mind to Ziliang, and had Wang Jian report it in full—whether any of this has reached you in outline, I cannot tell.

sentences.zh: 福慶方隆，國祚永始，若天假臣年，得預人位，唯當請降貂璫，以飾微軀，永侍天顏，以惟畢世，此臣之願也。

translations.literal: Fortune and blessing are on the rise, the throne newly established—if Heaven grants me years and I may share in rank among men, I would only ask to be lowered to the mink-and-scepter ranks to adorn this slight frame, forever to attend Your Majesty's countenance until life's end—that is my wish.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune is rising and the throne newly founded; if Heaven grants me years and a place among men, I would ask only to be lowered to the mink-and-scepter ranks, to dress this slight frame and attend your countenance to the end of my days—that is my wish.

sentences.zh: 服之不衷，猶為身災，況寵爵乎！

translations.literal: To wear what does not fit the heart is calamity for the person—how much more ennoblement and favor!
translations.idiomatic: To wear what the heart does not embrace is calamity for the body—how much more titles and grace!

sentences.zh: 殊榮厚恩，必誓以命請。

translations.literal: For extraordinary honor and thick grace I must vow with my life to petition.
translations.idiomatic: For extraordinary honor and thick grace I must petition with my life.

translations.idiomatic: Since the Song, provincial and commandery salaries and miscellaneous supplies had largely followed local produce, without fixed standard.

translations.idiomatic: long-standing uniformity; policy proceeds from one canon.

sentences.zh: 伏尋郡縣長尉俸祿之制，雖有定科，而其餘資給，復由風俗，東北異源，西南各緒，習以為常，因而弗變，緩之則莫非通規，澄之則靡不入罪。

translations.literal: I reflect that though the salary scales for commandery and county chiefs and assistants have fixed statutes, their other allowances again follow local custom—northeast with one source, southwest with another thread; habit makes it normal and it is not changed. Relax it and nothing fails to be the general rule; clarify it and nothing fails to be a crime.
translations.idiomatic: I find that though commandery and county chiefs and assistants have fixed salary statutes, their other allowances still follow local custom—one source in the northeast, another thread in the southwest; habit has made it normal and it goes unchanged. Relax enforcement and nothing is not the general practice; clarify it and nothing escapes being a crime.

sentences.zh: 殊非約法明章，先令後刑之謂也。

translations.literal: This is far from what is meant by making the law clear and issuing orders before punishments.
translations.idiomatic: That is far from making the law clear and issuing orders before punishments.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜使所在各條公用公田秩石迎送舊典之外，守宰相承，有何供調，尚書精加洗覈，務令優衷。

translations.literal: I hold that each locality should itemize public expenses, public fields, salary grain, and reception and escort beyond old precedent; the prefect and chancellor should answer for them, and whatever supplies are called for should be finely examined by the Masters of Writing, so that a balanced mean is secured.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that each locality should itemize public expenses, public fields, salary grain, and reception and escort beyond old precedent; prefect and chancellor should answer for them, and whatever supplies are demanded should be finely audited by the Masters of Writing until a balanced mean is reached.

translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan did not sit in on court business, yet in confidential counsel his words were often trusted and adopted.

translations.idiomatic: When mourning was completed, he was made palace attendant.

translations.literal: How much more when territory matches former measure and merit matches past pattern—though heavenly kinship has its root, circumstance deepens affection.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when territory matches former measure and merit matches past pattern—though heavenly kinship has its root, circumstance deepens affection.

translations.literal: He memorialized in his own person, saying, 「Since my return to court I have reduced my ceremonial sabers; the dozen-odd sword-bearers at my side I have reduced as well—only on distant journeys outside the city might they appear again for a time; I also go without them when entering the halls.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized in his own person, saying, 「Since my return to court I have cut back my ceremonial sabers; the dozen-odd sword-bearers at my side I have cut back as well—only on distant journeys outside the city might they appear again for a time; I also go without them when entering the halls.

translations.idiomatic: The attendants I now keep at my side are two warrior-guards on the carriage hubs, two white-uniform men—in all some seventy or eighty.

translations.idiomatic: I have never heard anyone speak of this.

translations.literal: I myself would not leave the princes without guards—how much less you!
translations.idiomatic: I myself would not leave the princes without guards—how much less you!

translations.literal: Riding such conveyances in a private garden is no cause for doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Riding such conveyances in a private garden is no cause for doubt.

sentences.zh: 郊外鳴角及合扇并拂，先乃有，不復施用，此來甚久。

translations.literal: Horns outside the city, folding screens, and fly-whisks existed before but are no longer used; that has been so for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Horns outside the city, folding screens, and fly-whisks existed before but are no longer used; that has been so for a long time.

sentences.zh: 凡在鎮自異還京師，先廣州乃立鼓吹，交部遂有輦事，隨時而改，亦復有可得依舊者。

translations.literal: Whenever one returns from a post in a distant region to the capital, custom changes with the times—Guang province first established a drum-and-pipe escort, Jiaozhi then had litter service; some things can still be followed as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever one returns from a distant post to the capital, custom changes with the times—Guang province first established a drum-and-pipe escort, Jiaozhi then had litter service; some things can still be followed as of old.

translations.idiomatic: If you have doubts, take measure with Wang Jian and the others, but see that the rites of subject and minister are not lost—that is enough.」

translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again, saying, 「I am slow to know how to comport myself and ignorant in what to ask when in doubt; I have often seen common clansmen who assist with edicts wearing cloth sandals and did not think it strange.

sentences.zh: 臣在西朝拜王，儀飾悉依宋武陵事例，有二鄣扇，仍此下都，脫不為疑。

translations.literal: When I paid court in the west my ceremonial accoutrements all followed the Song precedent of Prince Wu of Mount Wuling; I had two shield-screens and brought them down to the capital—I did not think that suspect.
translations.idiomatic: When I paid court in the west my ceremonial accoutrements all followed the Song precedent of Prince Wu of Mount Wuling; I had two shield-screens and brought them down to the capital—I did not think that suspect.

sentences.zh: 小兒奴子，並青布袴衫，臣齋中亦有一人，意謂外庶所服，不疑與羊車相類。

translations.literal: My young servants all wear blue cloth trousers and jackets; I have one such man in my study as well—I took it to be dress of the outer common sort and did not suspect it resembled the goat-cart retinue.
translations.idiomatic: My young servants all wear blue cloth trousers and jackets; I have one such man in my study as well—I took it to be dress of the outer common sort and did not suspect it resembled the goat-cart retinue.

sentences.zh: 曲荷慈旨，今悉改易。

translations.literal: Graced by your kind instruction, I have now changed all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Graced by your kind instruction, I have now changed all of it.

sentences.zh: 臣昔在邊鎮，不無羽衞，自歸朝以來，便相分遣，俠轂、白直，格置三百許人，臣頃所引，不過一百。

translations.literal: Once, on the frontier, I did not lack armed escort; since returning to court I have sent men away in batches. For carriage-guards and white-clad runners the fixed quota is some three hundred, yet I now retain barely a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier I once kept a full guard; since I came back to court I have been sending them away in batches. The establishment calls for some three hundred carriage-guards and white-clad runners, but I keep barely a hundred.

sentences.zh: 常謂京師諸王不煩牽仗，若郊外遠行，此所不論。

translations.literal: I had always held that princes in the capital need not drag along armed retinues; only for long journeys beyond the suburbs is that not discussed.
translations.idiomatic: I had always thought princes in the capital need not trail armed retinues—only when one rides far beyond the suburbs is that another matter.

sentences.zh: 有仗者非臣一人，所以不容方幅啟省，又因王儉備宣下情。

translations.literal: I am not the only one who keeps guards, so I could not properly memorialize to cut them; I also had Wang Jian convey my feelings below.
translations.idiomatic: I am not the only prince who keeps guards, so I could not bring myself to memorialize a full reduction; I had Wang Jian speak for me instead.

sentences.zh: 臣出入榮顯，禮容優泰，第宇華曠，事乖素約，雖宋之遺製，恩處有在，猶深非服之慙。

translations.literal: My comings and goings are glorious, my ritual bearing lavish, my mansion spacious—this strays from my plain pledge. Though Song left such precedent and favor has its place, I am deeply ashamed not to wear it comfortably.
translations.idiomatic: My comings and goings are splendid, my bearing ceremonious, my mansion vast—all of it at odds with the modest life I pledged. Song left such precedents, and grace has its reasons, yet I am ashamed I cannot bear them with ease.

sentences.zh: 威衞之請，仰希曲照。

translations.literal: On the request for armed guards, I hope for your gracious approval.
translations.idiomatic: As to my request to reduce my guard, I beg your gracious leave.

translations.idiomatic: 」 The emperor replied, "Men who relay edicts are palace household staff—there is nothing to suspect in that.

sentences.zh: 鄣扇吾識及以來未見，故有敕耳。

translations.literal: As for screen-fans—I have known you since we were young and never seen them; that is why there was an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Screen-fans—I have known you since boyhood and never saw you with them; that is why I sent word.

sentences.zh: 小兒奴子，本非嫌也。

translations.literal: Your boy-servants were never suspect.
translations.idiomatic: Your boy-servants were never in question.

sentences.zh: 吾有所聞，豈容不敕汝知，令物致議耶。

translations.literal: If I heard something, how could I fail to tell you, so that others would gossip?"
translations.idiomatic: If something reached my ears, would I not tell you rather than let the world talk?"

sentences.zh: 吾已有敕，汝一人不省俠轂，但牽之。

translations.literal: I have already ordered—as for you alone, do not cut the carriage-guards; just keep them.
translations.idiomatic: I have already ordered it—for you alone, do not cut your carriage-guards; keep them.

sentences.zh: 吾昨不通仗事，儉已道，吾即令荅，不煩有此啟。

translations.literal: Yesterday I was not informed of the escort matter—Jian already spoke; I ordered a reply at once. No need for this memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday the escort matter never reached me—Jian had already spoken, and I ordered an answer at once. You need not memorialize again.

translations.idiomatic: When we have time to talk, I will tell you a thing or two more."

sentences.zh: 又啟曰：「違遠侍宴，將踰一紀，憂苦閒之。

translations.literal: He memorialized again: "Far from attending banquets—nearly twelve years—grief and sorrow filled the intervals.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "I have been far from your banquets for nearly twelve years, and sorrow filled the spaces between.

sentences.zh: 始得開顏。

translations.literal: Only now may I uncloud my face.
translations.idiomatic: Only now may I let my face clear.

sentences.zh: 近頻侍座，不勝悲喜。

translations.literal: Lately I have often sat beside you—joy and sorrow beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have often sat at your side—joy and grief more than I can bear.

translations.idiomatic: (Read: zhan.)

sentences.zh: 〔沾〕飲過量，實欲仰示恩狎，令自下知見，以杜游塵。

translations.literal: Drinking beyond measure—truly I wished to show your affection above, so those below would see it and idle gossip would be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: I drank too much—only to show how close you hold me, so those below would see it and idle talk would die away.

sentences.zh: 陛下留恩子弟，此情何異，外物政自彊生閒節，聲其厚薄。

translations.literal: Your kindness to your sons and younger brothers—how is this feeling different? Outsiders will on their own inflate petty rumors and sound out who favors whom.
translations.idiomatic: Your love for your brothers and sons is the same in every case; outsiders will invent petty slights on their own and trumpet who is favored and who is not.

sentences.zh: 伏度或未上簡。

translations.literal: I suspect this may not have reached you in brief.
translations.idiomatic: I fear this may never have reached you in brief.

sentences.zh: 臣前在東田，承恩過醉，實思歎往秋之謗，故言啟至切，亦令羣物聞之，伏願已照此心。

translations.literal: Once at the Eastern Fields I received grace and drank too deep—truly I meant to sigh over last autumn's slander; hence my memorial was so urgent, also that the crowd might hear. I hope you have seen this heart.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the Eastern Fields you honored me and I drank too deep—I meant to answer last autumn's slander, which is why my words were so sharp and why I let the court hear them. I pray you have read my heart.

sentences.zh: 前侍幸順之宅，臣依常乘車至仗後，監伺不能示臣可否，便互競啟

translations.idiomatic: He heard that my carriage had pressed upon the imperial yellow canopy and banners, as if to strike them.

sentences.zh: 推此用意，亦何容易。

translations.literal: To infer intent from this—is that so easy?
translations.idiomatic: To read intent into that—is it so simple?

sentences.zh: 仰賴慈明，即賜垂敕；

translations.literal: Trusting in your merciful clarity, grant your decree at once;
translations.idiomatic: I rely on your clear mercy—grant your decree at once;

sentences.zh: 不爾，臣終不知闇貽此累。

translations.literal: otherwise I would never have known I darkly brought on this trouble.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise I would never have known I had stumbled into this blame in the dark.

sentences.zh: 比日禁斷整密，此自常理，外聲乃云起臣在華林，輒捉御刀，因此更嚴，度情推理，必不容爾，為復上啟知耳。

translations.literal: Lately prohibitions have been strict—that is natural—but outside rumor says it began with me in Hualin seizing the imperial guard sword, hence the tightening. Reasoning from feeling, it surely cannot be so; I memorialize only so you may know.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the bans have grown tight, as they should—but rumor outside says it began when I seized an imperial guard sword in Hualin, and the rules grew harsher still. Judged by reason, that cannot be; I write only so you may know.

sentences.zh: 但風塵易至，和會實難，伏願猶憶臣石頭所啟，無生閒縫。

translations.literal: Yet gossip rises easily and harmony is hard; I beg you still recall my memorial at Shitou—let no idle crack appear.
translations.idiomatic: Gossip comes quickly, concord with difficulty; I beg you remember what I wrote at Shitou—let no idle seam open between us.

sentences.zh: 比閑侍無次，略附茹亮口宣。

translations.literal: Lately, with nothing urgent while attending, I append Ru Liang's oral relay briefly.
translations.idiomatic: With nothing urgent in these idle audiences, I add Ru Liang's oral message in brief.

sentences.zh: 臣由來華素，已具上簡，每欲存衷，意慮不周，或有乖當。

translations.literal: I have always been lavish—already set out above in brief; each time I mean to keep the middle way, my thoughts fall short, and something may miss the mark.
translations.idiomatic: I have always lived in splendor, as I said above; each time I mean to hold the mean, my mind falls short, and something may go awry.

sentences.zh: 且臣五十之年，為翫幾時，為此亦復不能以理內自

translations.literal: And at fifty, how long is there for pleasure? For this I truly cannot restrain myself inwardly by reason alone
translations.idiomatic: At fifty, how many years of delight remain? For this I truly cannot school myself inwardly by reason alone

sentences.zh: 北第舊邸，本自甚華，臣改脩正而已，小小製置，已自仰簡。

translations.literal: The old northern residence was splendid to begin with—I only renovated it; the small fittings have already been submitted for your review.
translations.idiomatic: The northern mansion was grand to begin with; I only put it in order. The small appointments have already been laid before you.

sentences.zh: 往歲收合得少雜材，并蒙賜故板，啟榮內許作小眠齋，始欲成就，皆補接為辦，無乖格製，要是檉柏之華，一時新淨。

translations.literal: Last year I gathered a little mixed timber and was also granted old planks, and memorialized to build a small sleeping studio inside Qirong—just as it was to be finished, all was patched and fitted out, without breaking regulations; it was only the splendor of tamarisk and cypress, newly clean for a time.
translations.idiomatic: Last year I collected a little scrap timber and was also given old planks; I asked leave to build a small sleeping studio in the Qirong quarters. Just as it was nearly done, everything was patched and fitted—within the rules, but tamarisk and cypress made it briefly bright and new.

sentences.zh: 東府又有齋，亦為華屋。

translations.literal: The Eastern Residence also has a studio—likewise a splendid hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Residence has a studio too—another fine hall.

sentences.zh: 而臣頓有二處住止，下情竊所未安。

translations.literal: Yet I suddenly have two places to live—I feel privately uneasy below.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I suddenly have two dwellings, and it sits uneasily with me.

sentences.zh: 訊訪東宮玄圃，乃有柏屋，製甚古拙，內中無此齋，臣乃欲壞取以奉太子，非但失之於前，且補接既多，不可見移，亦恐外物或為異論，不審可有垂許送東府齋理否？

translations.literal: I inquired about the Eastern Palace's Mystic Enclosure Garden and found a cypress hall, very plain and old in make, with nothing inside like this studio; I wished to dismantle mine and offer it to the crown prince—not only a loss to what was before, but having been much patched and joined, it cannot be moved in view; I also fear outsiders might raise talk—may I beg permission to send the Eastern Residence studio instead?
translations.idiomatic: I asked after the crown prince's Mystic Enclosure and found only a cypress hall, plain and old, with nothing like this studio within. I thought to tear mine down for him—but that would undo what is already done, and with so much patching it cannot be moved in plain sight; outsiders might talk. May I beg leave to give the Eastern Residence studio instead?

sentences.zh: 臣公家住止，率爾可安，臣之今啟，實無意識，亦無言者，太子亦不知臣有此屋，政以東宮無，而臣自處之，體不宜爾爾。

translations.literal: My official household can make do casually; this memorial truly has no design, and none speak of it—the crown prince does not know I have this hall; only because the Eastern Palace lacks one while I keep two, the form is unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: My public household can manage well enough; this memorial has no hidden aim, and no one prompted it—the crown prince does not even know I have this hall. Only because his palace lacks such a room while I keep two does the thing sit wrong.

sentences.zh: 所啟蒙允，臣便當敢成第屋，安之不疑。

translations.literal: If you grant what I memorialized, I will dare finish the mansion and rest in it without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: If you grant what I ask, I will finish the mansion and live in it without another thought.

sentences.zh: 陛下若不照體臣心，便當永廢不脩。

translations.literal: If you do not see my heart's intent, I will abandon repair forever.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not read my heart, I will never build again.

sentences.zh: 臣自謂今啟非但是自處宜然，實為微臣往事，伏願必垂降許。

translations.literal: I hold this memorial is not only fitting for my station but answers to a petty minister's past—I beg you must grant it.
translations.idiomatic: I believe this request is not only right for my place but settles an old debt of mine as a humble servant—I beg you grant it.

sentences.zh: 伏見以諸王舉貨，屢降嚴旨，少拙營生，已應上簡。

translations.literal: I see that princes raising loans has drawn repeated stern edicts; my slight clumsiness at making a living should already be on your desk.
translations.idiomatic: I see how often you have sternly forbidden princes to borrow; my small awkwardness at earning a living must already be known to you.

sentences.zh: 府州郡邸舍，非臣私有，今巨細所資，皆是公潤，臣私累不少，未知將來罷州之後，或當不能不試學營覓以自贍。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county lodges are not my private property; all I draw on large or small is public surplus—I have no small private means; I do not know whether after leaving office I may have to try learning to earn my bread.
translations.idiomatic: The lodges in prefecture and county are not mine; everything I use, great or small, comes from public surplus. My private means are thin. When I leave office I may have to learn, however late, how to feed myself.

sentences.zh: 連年惡疾餘，顧影單回，無事畜聚，唯逐手為樂耳。

translations.literal: Years of grave illness leave me—turning to my shadow alone—without stores; I take only what comes to hand as my joy.
translations.idiomatic: Years of grave illness leave me alone with my shadow, without stores; I take only what comes to hand for comfort.

sentences.zh: 凡諸普敕，此意可尋，當不關汝一人也。

translations.literal: For all general edicts, this intent can be found—it surely concerns not you alone.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever general orders apply, you can read the intent in them—they are not aimed at you alone.

sentences.zh: 宜有敕事，吾亦必道，頃見汝自更委悉，書不欲多及。

translations.literal: When edicts are needed I will certainly say so; lately I have seen you lay things out yourself in detail—I do not wish the letter to go further.
translations.idiomatic: When there is something to decree, I will say it; lately you explain yourself well enough—I do not want the letter to run on.

sentences.zh: 屋事慎勿彊厝此意，白澤亦當不解何意爾。」

translations.idiomatic: As for the house, do not press the point—Baize will not understand your reasoning either."

sentences.zh: 三年，文惠太子講孝經畢，〔嶷〕求解太傅，不許。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Crown Prince Wenhui finished lecturing on the Classic of Filial Piety, [Yi] petitioned to resign as Grand Tutor and was refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Crown Prince Wenhui finished his lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, [Yi] asked to be released as Grand Tutor; the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 皇孫婚竟，又陳解。

translations.literal: When the imperial grandson's marriage was concluded, he again submitted a petition to resign.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial grandson's wedding was over, Xiao Yi again petitioned to resign his offices.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「公惟德惟行，無所厝辭。

translations.literal: An edict said: 「Lord, in virtue and in conduct alike, there is nowhere to set words aside.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, 「In virtue and in conduct you leave nothing to refuse.

sentences.zh: 且魯且衞，其誰與二。

translations.literal: Like Lu, like Wei—who ranks second to you?
translations.idiomatic: You stand with Lu and Wei—who stands beside you as second?

sentences.zh: 方式範當時，流聲史籍。

translations.literal: Your manner models the age; your name flows through the histories.
translations.idiomatic: Your bearing is the measure of the age; your name will run in the histories.

sentences.zh: 豈容屢秉撝謙，以乖期寄。

translations.literal: How can you again and again take up false modesty and fall short of what we expect?
translations.idiomatic: How can you keep clasping showy humility and fail what we have set upon you?

translations.literal: 」Yi often feared the fullness of fortune, and again because of
