sentences.zh: 〔宮〕宴，求解揚州授竟陵王子良。

translations.literal: a palace banquet, petitioned to relinquish Yang province and give it to Jingling Prince Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: a palace feast, asked to lay down Yang province and transfer it to Jingling Prince Xiao Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 上終不許，曰：「畢汝一世，無所多言。」

translations.literal: The emperor would not allow it and said, 「To the end of your life—no more of this talk.」
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear of it and said, 「For the rest of your life—say no more of it.」

sentences.zh: 世祖即位後，頻發詔拜陵，不果行。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu took the throne, he repeatedly issued edicts to worship at the imperial tombs but could not carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu acceded, he often ordered tomb worship but could never go himself.

sentences.zh: 遣嶷拜陵，還過延陵季子廟，觀沸井，有水牛突部伍，直兵執牛推問，不許，取絹一疋橫繫牛角，放歸其家。

translations.literal: He sent Yi to worship at the tombs. On the return he passed the shrine of Master Ji of Yanling and viewed the boiling spring. A water buffalo charged into the ranks; straight soldiers seized the beast to push and question it. Yi would not allow it, took a bolt of silk, bound it across the horns, and sent it home.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xiao Yi to worship at the tombs. Coming back he stopped at the shrine of Master Ji of Yanling and looked at the boiling spring. A water buffalo charged his escort; palace guards seized the beast to beat and question it. Yi forbade them, took a bolt of silk, lashed it across the horns, and let the animal go home.

sentences.zh: 為治存寬厚，故得朝野歡心。

translations.literal: In governance he kept to lenience and breadth, and so won the hearts of court and countryside alike.
translations.idiomatic: In rule he stayed lenient and broad, and court and countryside alike gave him their hearts.

sentences.zh: 四年，唐㝢之賊起，啟上曰：「此段小寇，出於兇愚，天網宏罩，理不足論。

translations.literal: In year 4 the rebel Tang Yuzhi rose. Yi memorialized the throne: 「This trifling banditry springs from violent folly; Heaven's net spans wide—reason need not dwell on it.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the outlaw Tang Yuzhi rose. Yi wrote, 「This petty trouble comes of brutish folly; Heaven's net is vast—it is hardly worth arguing.

sentences.zh: 但聖明御世，幸可不爾，比藉聲聽，皆云有由而然。

translations.literal: Yet in a sage reign one ought not to have it so; listening to rumor, all say there is cause behind it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet under a sage reign it ought not to be so; by rumor and report, everyone says there is a reason for it.

sentences.zh: 豈得不仰啟所懷，少陳心款。

translations.literal: How can I fail to lay my thoughts before you and speak my heart a little?
translations.idiomatic: How can I not lay what I feel before you and open my heart, if only a little?

sentences.zh: 山海崇深，臣獲保安樂，公私情願，於此可見。

translations.literal: Mountains and seas stand high and deep; I enjoy peace and safety—my public and private wish is plain.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains and seas are high and deep; I have been kept in peace and ease—my wish for state and for self is plain.

sentences.zh: 齊有天下，歲月未久，澤沾萬民，其實未多，百姓猶險，懷惡者眾。

translations.literal: Qi has held the realm not long; grace has not yet soaked the myriad people. The people are still hard, and many harbor ill will.
translations.idiomatic: Qi has held the realm only a short while; favor has not yet soaked the people. The common folk are still hard, and many nurse malice.

sentences.zh: 陛下曲垂流愛，每存優旨。

translations.literal: Your Majesty bends flowing love; you always keep a gentle tone.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty bends a flowing love and always keeps a gentle word.

sentences.zh: 但頃小大士庶，每以小利奉公，不顧所損者大，

translations.literal: Yet lately, great and small alike, each for a small gain serves the state and ignores the greater loss,
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately, high and low, each for a trifling gain serves the state and never weighs the greater harm,

translations.literal: (flog)
translations.idiomatic: (flog)

sentences.zh: 〔擿〕籍檢工巧，督卹簡小塘，藏丁匿口，凡諸條制，實長怨府。

translations.literal: registry checks of artisans, supervision of levies on ponds, hiding households and mouths—all such rules truly breed a treasury of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: exposing registries, inspecting craftsmen, pressing levies on ponds, hiding households and mouths—every such rule truly swells the house of resentment.

sentences.zh: 此目前交利，非天下大計。

translations.literal: This is immediate profit, not the great plan of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: This is profit for the moment, not the great reckoning of the realm.

sentences.zh: 一室之中，尚不可精，㝢宙之內，何可周

translations.literal: In one room exactitude is impossible; within the cosmos how can one comprehensively
translations.idiomatic: In one room you cannot be exact; in all the world how can you survey

translations.literal: (inspect)
translations.idiomatic: (inspect)

translations.literal: scrutinize all.
translations.idiomatic: every corner?

sentences.zh: 公家何嘗不知民多欺巧，古今政以不可細碎，故不為此，實非乖理。

translations.literal: The state has never failed to know the people are full of deceit; governments ancient and modern have held that minute regulation cannot work, and so refrained—this is not against reason.
translations.idiomatic: The state has never not known how deceitful the people are; rulers old and new have held that the fine print cannot govern, and so they did not do this—it is not against reason.

sentences.zh: 但識理者百不有一，陛下弟兒大臣，猶不皆能伏理，況復天下悠悠萬品。

translations.literal: But hardly one in a hundred grasps reason; even your Majesty's brothers and great ministers do not all submit to reason—how much more the endless kinds of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: But hardly one man in a hundred knows reason; even your Majesty's brothers and great ministers do not all bow to reason—how much more the endless kinds under heaven.

sentences.zh: 怨積聚黨，兇迷相類，止於一處，何足不除，脫復多所，便成紜紜。

translations.literal: Resentment piles up and parties form; violent folly finds its kind. Confined to one place, why not wipe it out? If it spreads widely, chaos follows.
translations.idiomatic: Grievance gathers into factions; the violent and deluded flock together. In one place alone, why could it not be cleared? If it breaks out in many places, all becomes confusion.

sentences.zh: 久欲上啟，閑侍無因，謹陳愚管，伏願特留神思。

translations.literal: Long I have wished to speak; at leisure I had no opening. I venture my shallow counsel and beg your special attention.
translations.idiomatic: Long I have wished to speak to you; in quiet attendance I had no opening. I venture this foolish counsel and beg you to weigh it with care.

sentences.zh: 」上荅曰：「欺巧那可容！

translations.literal: 」The emperor replied: 「Deceit—how can it be tolerated!
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor answered, 「Deceit—how can that be borne!

sentences.zh: 宋世混亂，以為是不？

translations.literal: You think Song's chaos came from this?
translations.idiomatic: Do you think Song's chaos came from that?

sentences.zh: 蚊蟻何足為憂，已為義勇所破，官軍昨至，今都應散滅。

translations.literal: Gnats and ants—why fret? The righteous militia has already broken them; the government army arrived yesterday; all should be scattered by now.
translations.idiomatic: Midges and ants—why worry? The righteous militia has already broken them; the government army came yesterday; by now they should all be scattered.

sentences.zh: 吾政恨其不辦大耳，亦何時無亡命邪。

translations.literal: I only regret they did not make a grand revolt; when has there ever been a lack of outlaws?
translations.idiomatic: I only wish they had made something grand of it; when was there ever no outlaw?

sentences.zh: 」後乃詔聽復籍注。

translations.literal: 」Later an edict allowed restoring registry records.
translations.idiomatic: 」Only later did an edict allow restoring registry entries.

sentences.zh: 五年，進位大司馬。

translations.literal: In year 5 he was advanced to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was promoted to Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 八年，給皁輪車。

translations.literal: In year 8 he was given a black-wheeled carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was granted a carriage with black wheels.

sentences.zh: 尋加中書監，固讓。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made Director of the Secretariat but firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named Director of the Secretariat and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 嶷身長七尺八寸，善持容範，文物衞從，禮冠百僚，每出入殿省，皆瞻望嚴肅。

translations.literal: Yi stood seven feet eight inches; he bore himself with exemplary dignity, his insignia and escort putting all officials in the shade. Whenever he entered or left the palace halls, all looked on with solemn respect.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi stood seven feet eight inches tall. He held his bearing with grace; his insignia and escort outshone every officer. Whenever he passed through the palace halls, all who saw him looked on in solemn awe.

sentences.zh: 自以地位隆重，深懷退素，北宅舊有園田之美，乃盛脩理之。

translations.literal: Seeing his station so weighty, he cherished withdrawal and plainness; the north residence had once fine gardens and fields, and he had them greatly restored.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing how weighty his place had become, he turned his heart to withdrawal and plain living; the north mansion had once held fine gardens and fields, and he had them restored on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 七年，啟求還第，上令世子子廉代鎮東府。

translations.literal: In year 7 he petitioned to return to his residence; the emperor had the heir son Zilian replace him at the Eastern Mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he asked to go back to his mansion; the emperor had his heir Xiao Zilian take his place at the Eastern Mansion.

sentences.zh: 上數幸嶷第。

translations.literal: The emperor often visited Yi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited Xiao Yi's mansion.

sentences.zh: 宋長寧陵𡑞道出第前路，上曰：「我便是入他冢墓內尋人。

translations.literal: The spirit way of Emperor Ming's Changning tomb ran before the residence gate. The emperor said, 「I am really going into someone else's graveyard to call on a friend.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit road of Emperor Ming's Changning tomb ran past the gate of the mansion. The emperor said, 「I am walking into another man's graveyard to find a friend.

sentences.zh: 」乃徙其表闕騏驎於東崗上。

translations.literal: 」He had the spirit gate and qilin moved to the eastern hill.
translations.idiomatic: 」So he had the spirit gate and the qilin moved to the eastern ridge.

sentences.zh: 騏驎及闕，形勢甚巧，宋孝武於襄陽致之，後諸帝王陵皆模範而莫及也。

translations.literal: The qilin and gate were wonderfully wrought; Emperor Xiaowu of Song had them brought from Xiangyang; later imperial tombs all took them as models but none matched.
translations.idiomatic: The qilin and the gate were marvelously wrought; Emperor Xiaowu of Song had had them brought from Xiangyang; later imperial tombs all took them as models, yet none equaled them.

sentences.zh: 永明末，車駕數游幸，唯嶷陪從，上出新林苑，同輦夜歸，至宮門，嶷下輦辭出，上曰：「今夜行，無使為尉司所呵也。

translations.literal: Late in Yongming the imperial carriage often went touring; only Yi accompanied him. The emperor left Xinlin Park and returned by night in the same carriage. At the palace gate Yi stepped down to take leave. The emperor said, 「On a night ride like this, don't let the watch be scolding us.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yongming the emperor often went touring; only Xiao Yi went with him. Once he left Xinlin Park and rode back by night in the same carriage. At the palace gate Yi stepped down to withdraw. The emperor said, 「On a night run like this, see that the watch does not scold us.

sentences.zh: 」嶷對曰：「京輦之內，皆屬臣州，願陛下不垂過慮。

translations.literal: 」Yi answered, 「Within the capital all falls under my province—Your Majesty need not worry overmuch.
translations.idiomatic: 」Yi answered, 「Within the capital all lies in my province—Your Majesty need not trouble yourself.

sentences.zh: 」上大笑。

translations.literal: 」The emperor laughed aloud.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor laughed long.

sentences.zh: 上謀北伐，以虜所獻氈車賜嶷。

translations.literal: When the emperor planned a northern campaign, he gave Yi the felt carriage presented by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned a northern campaign, he gave Xiao Yi the felt carriage the barbarians had presented.

sentences.zh: 每幸第清除，不復屏人。

translations.literal: Whenever he visited the residence he cleared the way and no longer screened people away.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he visited the mansion he cleared the halls and no longer kept people at a screen.

sentences.zh: 上敕外監曰：「我往大司馬第，是還家耳。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the outer steward: 「When I go to the Grand Marshal's residence, I am simply going home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the outer steward, 「When I go to the Grand Marshal's house, I am only going home.

sentences.zh: 」妃庾氏常有疾，瘳，上幸〔嶷邸〕，後堂設金石樂，宮人畢至。

translations.literal: 」 His consort, the Lady Yu, had often been ill; when she recovered, the emperor visited [Yi's residence]; in the rear hall bell-and-stone music was set out and all palace women attended.
translations.idiomatic: 」 His consort Lady Yu had long been unwell; when she mended, the emperor came to Yi's residence, bell-and-stone music in the rear hall and every palace woman present.

sentences.zh: 每臨幸，輒極日盡歡。

translations.literal: On every visit he would revel to the day's end.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he came, the feasting ran until the light failed.

sentences.zh: 嶷謂上曰：「古來言願陛下壽偕南山，或稱萬歲，此殆近貌言，如臣所懷，實願陛下極壽百年亦足矣。

translations.literal: Yi said to the emperor, 「Since antiquity men have said, "May Your Majesty's years match the southern mountain," or called out "Ten thousand years"—such words border on flattery; in my heart I truly wish Your Majesty a full century of life, and that would be enough.
translations.idiomatic: Yi told the emperor, 「Men since old times say, "May Your Majesty live as long as the southern mountain," or shout "Ten thousand years"—that is nearly empty praise. What I truly wish is that Your Majesty reach a full century, and no more.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「百年復何可得，止得東西一百，於事亦濟。」

translations.literal: 」 The emperor said, 「How could a full century be had? East and west together make a hundred—and that will do."」
translations.idiomatic: 」 The emperor said, 「Who can have a full century? East plus west is a hundred—and that will serve."」

sentences.zh: 十年，上封嶷諸子，舊例千戶，嶷欲五子俱封，啟減人五百戶。

translations.literal: In year 10 the emperor enfeoffed Yi's sons; by old precedent each received a thousand households; Yi wanted all five sons enfeoffed together and memorialized to reduce each by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the emperor enfeoffed Yi's sons—by old rule, a thousand households each. Yi asked that all five be enfeoffed at once and memorialized to cut five hundred households from each grant.

sentences.zh: 其年疾篤，表解職，不許，賜錢百萬營功德。

translations.literal: That year, gravely ill, he memorialized to resign his posts; this was refused, and a million cash was granted to fund meritorious works.
translations.idiomatic: That year, deathly ill, he asked in a memorial to be released from office; the throne refused and gave a million cash for pious works.

sentences.zh: 嶷又啟曰：「臣自嬰今患，亟降天臨，醫徙術官，泉開藏府，慈寵優渥，備極人臣。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized again, saying, 「Since I fell into this illness Heaven's grace has descended again and again—physicians moved, medical officials summoned, treasuries opened; favor and kindness beyond measure, to the utmost a subject may receive.
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrote again: 「Since this sickness took me, Heaven's grace has come again and again—physicians posted, healers called, the vaults opened. Kindness has heaped upon me past what any subject may bear.

sentences.zh: 生年疾迫，遽陰無幾。

translations.literal: My years press upon me in sickness; the shadow of death is not far.
translations.idiomatic: My span is cramped by disease; the dark is close.

sentences.zh: 願陛下審賢與善，極壽蒼旻，彊德納和，為億兆御。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty discern the worthy and practice goodness, reach the utmost span beneath Heaven, strengthen virtue and welcome harmony, and rule the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty choose the worthy and do good, live out the sky's full term, gather strength and welcome peace, and steer the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 臣命違昌數，奄奪恩憐，長辭明世，伏涕嗚咽。

translations.literal: My fate turns from prosperity's count; grace and favor are torn away; I take long leave of this bright world and bow my face in weeping.
translations.idiomatic: My lot has turned from fortune's number; favor is snatched away. I leave the bright world for long, and bow my face in sobs.

sentences.zh: 」薨，年四十九。

translations.literal: 」 He died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: 」 He died at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 其日，上再視疾，至薨，乃還宮。

translations.literal: That day the emperor visited his illness twice; only when Yi died did he return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor came twice to his sickbed; only after Yi died did he go back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「嶷明哲至親，勳高業始，德懋王朝，道光區縣，奄至薨逝，痛酷抽割，不能自勝，奈何奈何！

translations.literal: An edict read, 「Yi was wise and bright, close kin supreme; his merit rose at the founding of our enterprise, his virtue enriched the royal court, his ways illumined districts and counties—suddenly he has passed. Grief cuts like rending flesh; I cannot bear it—what is to be done, what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, 「Yi was clear-sighted and nearest kin; his merit stood at the birth of our rule, his virtue filled the court, his light spread through the districts—then suddenly he was gone. Pain tears like flaying; I cannot master myself—what is to be done, what is to be done!

sentences.zh: 今便臨哭。

translations.literal: I shall come at once to mourn beside him.
translations.idiomatic: I will go now to weep at his side.

sentences.zh: 九命之禮，宜備其制。

translations.literal: The rites of nine investitures should be provided in full.
translations.idiomatic: The ninefold honors should be given in full.

sentences.zh: 斂以衮冕之服，溫明祕器，命服一具，衣一襲，喪事一依漢東平王故事，大鴻臚持節護喪事，大官朝夕送奠。

translations.literal: For encoffining: robes of dragon and twelve symbols, the secret warmth-and-brightness vessel, one set of invested garments, one suit of clothes; funeral observances to follow the Han precedent of the King of Dongping; the Grand Herald to hold the staff and supervise the funeral; the Grand Provisioner to send offerings morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be dressed in dragon robes and twelve emblems, with the secret warmth-and-brightness vessel, one set of command robes, one suit of clothes. The funeral follows the Han King of Dongping. The Grand Herald shall hold the staff and oversee the rites; the Grand Provisioner shall send offerings morning and night.

sentences.zh: 大司馬、太傅二府文武悉停過葬。」

translations.literal: All civil and military officials of the Grand Marshal and Grand Tutor households shall cease work for the mourning period."」
translations.idiomatic: All civil and military officers of the Grand Marshal and Grand Tutor offices shall stop duty for the burial."」

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良啟上曰：「臣聞春秋所以稱王母弟者，以尊其所重故也。

translations.literal: The prince of Jingling, Ziliang, memorialized the emperor, saying, 「I have heard that the Spring and Autumn Annals calls one the king's mother's younger brother to honor what it esteems.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Jingling, Ziliang, wrote to the throne: 「I have heard that the Spring and Autumn calls a man the king's mother's younger brother because it honors what matters.

sentences.zh: 是以禮秩殊品，爵命崇異，在漢則梁王備出警入蹕之儀，在晉則齊王具殊服九命之贈。

translations.literal: Hence ritual rank uses special grades and titles bestow lofty distinctions—in Han the King of Liang had the full ceremony of emerging guard and entering royal barrier; in Jin the King of Qi received the special garments and gift of nine investitures.
translations.idiomatic: So ritual rank has its special grades and titles their lofty differences—in Han the King of Liang had the full guard when he went out and the barrier when he entered; in Jin the King of Qi received the extraordinary robes and the ninefold posthumous gift.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，尊親是闕，故致衮章之典，廢而不傳，寔由人缺其位，非禮虧省。

translations.literal: Since the southeast took the throne, esteem for close kin has been wanting, so the rite of dragon robes has lapsed and is no longer handed down—it is truly because men lacked the stature for the office, not because the rites themselves were diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Since the court moved south, honor for close kin has been thin, and the dragon-robe rite has died out—not because the ritual was cut back, but because no man filled the place.

sentences.zh: 齊王故事，與今不殊，締構王業，功迹不異，凡有變革隨時之宜者，政緣恩情有輕重，德義有厚薄，若事籌前規，禮無異則。

translations.literal: The precedents of Qi kings match the present case; they bound up our royal enterprise and their deeds are not different. Whenever change follows timely fitness, it is because affection has its weights and virtue its depth—if one measures against former statutes, the rites should be no different.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi kings' precedents match today: they wove the royal work and their deeds are the same. Changes that fit the time come from how deep affection runs and how thick virtue is—measured against old rules, the rites should not differ.

sentences.zh: 且梁、齊闕令終之美，猶饗褒贈之榮；

translations.literal: Moreover, the Kings of Liang and Qi lacked a beautiful end to their lives, yet still received the glory of posthumous honors;
translations.idiomatic: Even the Kings of Liang and Qi, who did not finish well, still won posthumous glory;

sentences.zh: 況故大司馬仁和著於天性，孝悌終於立身，節義表於勤王，寬猛彰於御物，奉上無艱劬之貌，接下無毀傷之容，淡矣止於清貞，無喜慍之色，悠然栖於靜默，絕馳競之聲。

translations.literal: how much more the late Grand Marshal, whose benevolence showed in his inborn nature, filial piety and brotherliness completed in his person, integrity and righteousness displayed in serving the throne, lenience and severity manifest in governing affairs—serving above without strain, receiving those below without wounding face—plainly dwelling in purity and constancy, without joy or anger on his countenance, calmly resting in silence, utterly without the noise of faction and scramble.
translations.idiomatic: how much more the late Grand Marshal, whose kindness was in his nature, whose filial piety and brotherly love shaped his life, whose constancy showed in serving the throne, whose balance of lenience and severity showed in ruling men—above him no look of toil, below him no face wounded—plain in purity, without joy or anger on his face, at rest in silence, with no sound of rushing and rivalry.

sentences.zh: 詩云『靡不有初，鮮克有終』。

translations.literal: The Odes say, "Few do not have a beginning; few can keep to the end."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "Everything has a beginning; few keep an end."

sentences.zh: 夫終之者，理實為難，在於今行，無廢斯德。

translations.literal: To finish well is hard in truth; in what is done now, let this virtue not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: To end well is hard in the nature of things; in what we do now, do not waste this virtue.

sentences.zh: 東平樂於小善，河閒悅於詩書，勳績無聞，艱危不涉，尚致卓爾不羣，英聲萬代；

translations.literal: The King of Dongping delighted in small good deeds; the King of Hejian loved the classics and histories—no renown in merit, no peril endured—yet they still rose singular among their peers, their bright fame lasting ten thousand generations;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Dongping took joy in small kindnesses; the King of Hejian loved the Books and the Odes—no great deeds, no hard trials—yet they still stood alone, their names bright for ten thousand years;

sentences.zh: 況今協贊皇基，經綸霸始，功業高顯，清譽逾彰，富貴隆重，廉潔彌峻，等古形今，孰類茲美。

translations.literal: how much more he who aided the imperial foundation, wove the plans at the rise of our hegemony—deeds lofty and manifest, pure fame ever brighter, wealth and honor great yet integrity only sterner—matching past to present, who equals this excellence?
translations.idiomatic: how much more one who helped raise the throne, who shaped the realm at its founding—deeds high and clear, pure fame ever brighter, rank and riches heavy yet integrity only stricter—set old beside new, who matches this beauty?

sentences.zh: 臣愚忖度，未有斯例。

translations.literal: In my foolish reckoning, there has never been such a case.
translations.idiomatic: In my poor judgment, there is no precedent.

sentences.zh: 凡庶族同氣，愛睦尚少，豈有仰覩陛下垂友于之性若此者乎？

translations.literal: Among common clansmen, love and harmony are already rare—how could one look up and behold Your Majesty's brotherly affection such as this?
translations.idiomatic: Among ordinary kin, love between brothers is already scarce—who has ever seen Your Majesty's brotherly heart like this?

sentences.zh: 共起布衣，俱登天貴，生平遊處，何事不同，分甘均味，何珍不等，未常覩貌而天心不懽，見形而聖儀不悅。

translations.literal: You rose together from plain cloth and both ascended to heaven's nobility; in life's comings and goings nothing differed, in sharing sweet or sharing taste no treasure was unequal—never did the emperor's heart fail to rejoice at sight of his face, never did the sovereign's bearing fail to brighten at sight of his form.
translations.idiomatic: You rose from common cloth together and climbed to heaven's height; in life you shared every path, every sweet, every prize—never did the Son of Heaven see his face without joy, never his form without delight.

sentences.zh: 爰及臨危捨命，親瞻喘息，萬分之際，沒在聖目，號哭動乎天地，感慟驚乎鬼神，乃至撤膳移寢，坐泣遷旦，神儀損秏，隔宿改容，奉瞻聖顏，誰不悲悚，歷古所未聞，記籍所不載。

translations.literal: When he came to the crisis of life and death, Your Majesty watched his gasping breath; in the ten-thousandth of a moment he passed before the sacred eye—the wailing moved heaven and earth, the grief startled spirits and ghosts; you ceased meals and moved your couch, sat weeping until dawn, your sacred bearing wasted, your countenance changed overnight; all who gazed upon the sovereign's face—who was not stricken with sorrow and fear? Such things have never been heard through the ages, never recorded in annals.
translations.idiomatic: At the edge of death Your Majesty watched his breath; in the last fraction he vanished before the sacred eye—wailing that shook heaven and earth, grief that startled ghosts and spirits. You stopped your meals and moved your bed, sat weeping until dawn, your sacred bearing worn, your face changed overnight. Who looked on the sovereign's countenance without dread and sorrow? Never heard in all time, never written in any record.

sentences.zh: 既有若斯之大德，實不可見典服之贈不彰，如其脫致虧忘，追改為煩，不令千載之下，物有遺恨。

translations.literal: With virtue so great, it truly cannot be that the gift of canonical raiment should go unshown; if by mischance it were overlooked, later correction would be a burden, and under a thousand years' gaze regret would linger.
translations.idiomatic: With merit so vast, the gift of canonical robes must not go unseen; if it were missed by chance, to amend later would be pain, and a thousand years hence regret would remain.

sentences.zh: 其德不具美者，尚荷嘉隆之命；

translations.literal: Those whose virtue was not complete still received honors bright and grand;
translations.idiomatic: Men whose virtue was not whole still received splendid honors;

sentences.zh: 況事光先烈者，寧可缺茲盛典。

translations.literal: how much less one whose deeds illumine the former emperor—how could this great ceremony be wanting?
translations.idiomatic: how much less one whose deeds outshine the former age—how could this great rite be left out?

sentences.zh: 臣恐有識之人，容致其議。

translations.literal: Your servant fears men of judgment may offer criticism.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that men of sense may raise complaint.

sentences.zh: 且庶族近代桓溫、庾亮之類，亦降殊命，伏度天心，已當有在。」

translations.literal: Moreover, among lesser kin in recent times—men like Huan Wen and Yu Liang—extraordinary orders were also bestowed. I submit that Heaven's heart must already incline toward this."」
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in recent times even collateral lines—Huan Wen, Yu Liang, and the like—received special orders. I venture that Heaven's mind is already set."」

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「寵章所以表德，禮秩所以紀功。

translations.literal: Another edict read, 「Favors and badges proclaim virtue; ritual rank records merit.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, 「Honors show virtue; ritual rank records merit.

sentences.zh: 慎終追遠，前王之盛策，累行疇庸，列代之通誥。

translations.literal: To honor the dead and cherish the remote is the great policy of former kings; to amass deeds and rank service is the common decree of successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: To tend the dead and reach back to the distant is the great policy of ancient kings; to heap deeds and rank merit is the common charge of every age.

sentences.zh: 故使持節、都督揚南徐二州諸軍事、大司馬、領太子太傅、揚州刺史、新除中書監、豫章王嶷，體道秉哲，經仁緯義，挺清譽於弱齡，發韶風於早日，締綸覇業之初，翼讚皇基之始，孝睦著於鄉閭，忠諒彰乎邦邑。

translations.literal: The late Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the militaries of Yang and South Xuzhou, Grand Marshal, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, Governor of Yangzhou, newly appointed Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Yuzhang Yi embodied the Way and held wisdom, wove benevolence and bound righteousness, raised pure fame from tender years, sent forth the fair wind of their age from early days, bound the silken thread at the beginning of our hegemony, winged the royal foundation at its start—filial harmony renowned in hamlet and lane, loyal candor shining in town and district.
translations.idiomatic: The late Bearer of the Staff, commander of the armies of Yang and South Xuzhou, Grand Marshal, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, Governor of Yangzhou, newly made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Yuzhang Yi—he held the Way and wisdom, wove benevolence and bound righteousness, won clear fame in youth, sent forth fair renown in his early years, tied the founding cord at the start of our hegemony, winged the throne at the birth of the realm. Filial harmony shone in his village; loyal candor in his district.

sentences.zh: 及秉德論道，總牧神甸，七教必荷，六府咸理，振風潤雨，無諐於時候，卹民拯物，有篤於矜懷，雍容廊廟之華，儀形列郡之觀，神凝自遠，具瞻允集。

translations.literal: When he took up virtue and discussed the Way, overseeing the sacred demesne—seven teachings surely borne, six treasuries all ordered—stirring wind and moistening rain without fault to the seasons, comforting the people and rescuing things with deep compassion in his breast—graceful in the splendor of the court hall, a model for the gaze of many commanderies, spirit gathered from afar, all eyes and hopes assembled.
translations.idiomatic: When he bore virtue and spoke the Way, ruling the sacred heartland—seven teachings upheld, six offices in order—wind stirred and rain fell without fault to the seasons, the people eased and things rescued from deep compassion—graceful in the court's splendor, a model to the commanderies, his spirit drawing from afar, all eyes upon him.

sentences.zh: 朕友于之深，情兼家國，方授以神圖，委諸廟勝，緝頌九紘，陪禪五岳。

translations.literal: Our brotherhood was deep; feeling joined family and state. We were about to entrust him with the divine chart, commit to him the victories of the temple altar, weave praise across the nine cords of the realm, have him assist at the rite of the five peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Brotherly love ran deep; feeling joined house and realm. We were about to give him the sacred chart, entrust him with the temple's victories, weave praise through the nine realms, have him stand beside us at the rite of the five peaks.

sentences.zh: 天不憗遺，奄焉薨逝，哀痛傷惜，震慟乎厥心。

translations.literal: Heaven was not kind; suddenly he passed. Grief and pain shake our heart.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven was unkind; suddenly he was gone. Grief and pain shake the heart.

sentences.zh: 今先遠戒期，龜謀襲吉，宜加茂典，以協徽猷。

translations.literal: Now the season for ancestral rites draws near, the tortoise rites proclaim auspicious day—splendid ceremony should be added to harmonize with our great design.
translations.idiomatic: Now the season of the distant dead draws near, the tortoise rites show an auspicious day—grand honors should be added to match our great purpose.

sentences.zh: 可贈假黃鉞、都督中外諸軍事、丞相、揚州牧，綠綟綬，具九服錫命之禮，侍中、大司馬、太傅、王如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously grant: acting Yellow Battle-axe, Commander-in-Chief of all armies at court and in the provinces, Chancellor, Governor of Yangzhou, green sash and ribbon, full rites of nine garments and investiture-gift—the posts of Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, and Grand Tutor remain as prince.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be granted posthumously: acting Yellow Battle-axe, commander of all armies within and beyond the passes, Chancellor, Governor of Yangzhou, green sash and ribbon, the full nine-garment investiture rite—Palace Attendant, Grand Marshal, Grand Tutor, and prince as before.

sentences.zh: 給九旒鸞輅，黃屋左纛，虎賁班劍百人，轀輬車，前後部羽葆鼓吹，葬送儀依東平王故事。」

translations.literal: Grant the nine-tasselled phoenix chariot, yellow canopy and left banner, a hundred Tiger Guards with coupled swords, the bier-wagon, front and rear feather-canopies and drums and pipes—funeral rites per the Dongping King precedent."」
translations.idiomatic: Give the nine-tasselled phoenix carriage, yellow canopy and left banner, a hundred Tiger Guards with paired swords, the bier carriage, front and rear feather-canopies with drums and pipes—the funeral follows the King of Dongping."」

sentences.zh: 嶷臨終，召子子廉、子恪曰：「人生在世，本自非常，吾年已老，前路幾何。

translations.literal: At his end Yi summoned his sons Ziliang and Zike, saying, 「Human life is never ordinary; I am old—how much road remains?
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Yi called his sons Ziliang and Zike and said, 「Life among men is never sure; I am old—how much road is left?

sentences.zh: 居今之地，非心期所及。

translations.literal: To stand where I stand today was never what I foresaw in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: To stand where I stand now was never what I hoped for.

sentences.zh: 性不貪聚，自幼所懷，政以汝兄弟累多，損吾暮志耳。

translations.literal: By nature I do not hoard; this I have carried since youth—it is only that you brothers are so many and have worn down my late resolve.
translations.idiomatic: I was never greedy by nature—that is what I have held since boyhood. Only that you brothers are so many has worn down my wish for a quiet old age.

sentences.zh: 無吾

translations.literal: Without me,
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone,

translations.literal: After.
translations.idiomatic: After (emended from desire).

sentences.zh: 〔後〕，當共相勉厲，篤睦為先。

translations.literal: 〔After〕, you must together encourage one another and put steadfast harmony first.
translations.idiomatic: After I am gone, you must urge one another on and put brotherly harmony first.

sentences.zh: 才有優劣，位有通塞，運有富貧，此自然理，無足以相陵侮。

translations.literal: Talent has high and low, rank has smooth passage and blockage, fortune has rich and poor—this is natural principle; it is not enough to bully one another.
translations.idiomatic: Talent has its grades, office its open and blocked paths, fortune its rich and poor—natural law. That is no warrant to lord it over one another.

sentences.zh: 若天道有靈，汝等各自脩立，灼然之分無失也。

translations.literal: If the Way of Heaven has spirit, each of you cultivate and establish yourselves—clear distinctions will not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven is mindful, each of you must stand on your own merit—plain rank will not slip.

sentences.zh: 勤學行，守基業，治閨庭，尚閑素，如此足無憂患。

translations.literal: Study diligently and act, keep the family foundation, govern the inner household, esteem plain simplicity—so you will be free of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Work at learning and conduct, hold the estate, keep the inner house in order, value plain living—then you will have little to fear.

sentences.zh: 聖主儲皇及諸親賢，亦當不以吾沒易情也。

translations.literal: The sage sovereign, the crown prince, and all worthy kin should likewise not change their feeling because I am gone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, the heir apparent, and our worthy kinsmen should not, I trust, turn cold because I am dead.

sentences.zh: 三日施靈，唯香火、槃水、

translations.literal: For the three-day spirit installation, only incense, basin-water,
translations.idiomatic: For the three-day laying-in of the spirit, only incense, a basin of water,

translations.literal: (gan)
translations.idiomatic: (gan)

sentences.zh: 〔盂〕飯、酒脯、檳榔而已。

translations.literal: 〔yu〕 rice, wine and dried meat, betel nut—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: a bowl of rice, wine and dried meat, and betel—that is all.

sentences.zh: 朔望菜食一盤，加以甘菓，此外悉省。

translations.literal: On new and full moon, one tray of vegetarian food with sweet fruit added; omit all else.
translations.idiomatic: On the first and fifteenth, one dish of plain food with fruit besides; cut everything else.

sentences.zh: 葬後除靈，可施吾常所乘轝扇繖。

translations.literal: After the burial, when the spirit is removed, you may display my usual carriage screens and parasols.
translations.idiomatic: Once the tomb rites are done and the spirit table cleared, you may set out the screens and parasols from my usual carriage.

sentences.zh: 朔望時節，席地香火、槃水、酒脯、

translations.literal: On new and full moons and seasonal days, incense on the ground, basin-water, wine and dried meat,
translations.idiomatic: On new and full moons and the seasonal days, incense on the ground, a basin of water, wine and dried meat,

translations.literal: (gan)
translations.idiomatic: (gan)

sentences.zh: 〔盂〕飯、檳榔便足。

translations.literal: 〔yu〕 rice and betel will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: a bowl of rice and betel will do.

sentences.zh: 雖才愧古人，意懷粗亦有在，不以遺財為累。

translations.literal: Though my talent falls short of the ancients, my intention still has some substance—I do not wish wealth left behind to be a burden.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot match the men of old, yet something of my mind remains—I would not have spare wealth become your burden.

sentences.zh: 主衣所餘，小弟未婚，諸妹未嫁，凡應此用，本自茫然，當稱力及時，率有為辦。

translations.literal: What remains from the master of robes: my younger brother is unwed, my sisters unmarried; all such expenses were always uncertain—act according to means and time, and see that all is done.
translations.idiomatic: From the wardrobe office there is a surplus, but my brother is still unwed and my sisters still unbetrothed; such costs were never clear. Spend as means and season allow, and see everything through.

sentences.zh: 事事甚多，不復甲乙。

translations.literal: Matters are many; I will not list them one by one.
translations.idiomatic: There is more, but I will not go through it item by item.

sentences.zh: 棺器及墓中，勿用餘物為後患也。

translations.literal: In coffin fittings and the tomb, use no extra objects to cause trouble later.
translations.idiomatic: Put nothing extra in the coffin or the grave that may breed trouble later.

sentences.zh: 朝服之外，唯下鐵鐶刀一口。

translations.literal: Aside from court dress, place only one iron-ring knife below.
translations.idiomatic: Besides court robes, lay only a single iron-ringed knife beneath.

sentences.zh: 作冢勿令深，一一依格，莫過度也。

translations.literal: Do not make the mound deep; follow every regulation; do not exceed measure.
translations.idiomatic: Do not dig the tomb deep; follow the statute in every point and do not overdo it.

sentences.zh: 後堂樓可安佛，供養外國二僧，餘皆如舊。

translations.literal: The rear-hall tower may house a Buddha and support two foreign monks; the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: You may set a Buddha in the rear-hall tower and keep two monks from abroad; leave all else as it is.

sentences.zh: 與汝遊戲後堂船乘，吾所乘牛馬，送二宮及司徒，服飾衣裘，悉為功德。

translations.literal: The pleasure boats of the rear hall with which I played with you, my oxen and horses—send them to the Two Palaces and the Minister of Works; robes and furs, all as merit offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The rear-hall boats we used for sport, the cattle and horses I rode—give them to the Two Palaces and the minister of works; robes and furs, all for merit.

sentences.zh: 」子廉等號泣奉行。

translations.literal: 」Zilian and the others wept and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zilian and his brothers wept as they carried out every word.

sentences.zh: 世祖哀痛特至，至冬乃舉樂宴朝臣，上歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu grieved beyond measure; only in winter did he hold music and feast the court ministers—the emperor sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu mourned as never before; not until winter did he set music and feast his ministers—and still he broke into sobs.

sentences.zh: 諸王邸不得起樓臨瞰宮掖，上後登景陽，望見樓悲感，乃敕毀之。

translations.literal: Princely residences were forbidden to erect towers overlooking the palace quarters; later the emperor ascended Jingyang, saw a tower, was moved to grief, and ordered it destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were forbidden to raise towers that looked down on the palace; later the emperor climbed Jingyang, saw such a tower, grieved, and commanded it torn down.

sentences.zh: 薨後，第庫無見錢，世祖敕貨雜物服飾得數百萬，起集善寺，月給第見錢百萬，至上崩乃省。

translations.literal: After his death the mansion treasury held no cash on hand; the emperor ordered goods and dress sold for millions, built Jishan Temple, gave the residence a million cash each month—only when the emperor died was this withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: After he died there was not a coin in the house treasury; the emperor sold furnishings and dress for millions, founded Jishan Temple, and paid the mansion a million cash a month—only at his own death was the grant cut.

sentences.zh: 〔嶷〕性汎愛，不樂聞人過失，左右有投書相告，置鞾中，竟不視，取火焚之。

translations.literal: 〔Yi〕 was broad in love and disliked hearing people's faults; when attendants dropped letters accusing others he put them in his boot, never looked, and burned them over a fire.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ni loved widely and would not hear ill of anyone; if a servant slipped him an anonymous note, he tucked it in his boot unread and burned it at the lamp.

sentences.zh: 齋庫失火，燒荊州還資，評直三千餘萬，主局各杖數十而已。

translations.literal: The fast-day storehouse caught fire and burned the goods returned from Jing province—valued at more than thirty million; the clerks in charge were caned several dozen strokes each, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: The fasting-store caught fire and consumed the Jing tribute still in hand—thirty million and more by appraisal; the clerks in charge were flogged a few dozen strokes apiece, and that was the end of it.

sentences.zh: 羣吏中南陽樂藹、彭城劉繪、吳郡張稷最被親禮。

translations.literal: Among his staff, Le Yue of Nanyang, Liu Hui of Pengcheng, and Zhang Ji of Wu commandery were most honored.
translations.idiomatic: Of his officers, Le Yue of Nanyang, Liu Hui of Pengcheng, and Zhang Ji of Wu were closest to his favor.

sentences.zh: 藹與竟陵王子良牋曰：「道德以可久傳聲，風流以浸遠揮稱。

translations.literal: Yue wrote to Prince Ziliang of Jingling: 「Virtue transmits its fame through endurance; style and elegance win renown as they spread afar.
translations.idiomatic: Le Yue wrote to Xiao Ziliang, prince of Jingling: 「Virtue endures and so its name travels; grace goes deep and so its praise carries far.

sentences.zh: 雖復青簡締芳，未若玉石之不朽，飛翰圖藻，豈伊雕篆之無沫。

translations.literal: Though green bamboo binds fragrance, it is not like jade and stone that do not perish; flying brush and figured ornament—how could carved seal alone be without speck?
translations.idiomatic: Green bamboo may bind its perfume, yet jade and stone alone do not decay; brushwork and painted glory—can chisel and seal alone be spotless?

sentences.zh: 丞相沖粹表於天真，淵照殆乎機象。

translations.literal: The Chancellor's pure essence displayed in native truth; abyssal illumination nearly matched the trigrams.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor's purity showed in what he was by nature; his deep light nearly touched the signs of change.

sentences.zh: 經邦緯民之範，體國成務之規。

translations.literal: A model for ordering the state and weaving the people; a plan for embodying the realm and fulfilling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was the pattern for governing the realm and binding the people, the measure for holding the state and finishing its work.

sentences.zh: 故以業茂惟賢，功高則哲。

translations.literal: Therefore merit flourishes only in the worthy, and lofty achievement makes one wise.
translations.idiomatic: Hence merit thickens where worth gathers, and great deeds crown the sage.

sentences.zh: 神輝眇邈，叡算不追，感纏奉車，恨百留滯。

translations.literal: His spirit-light is dim and far; sagely reckoning cannot overtake it—grief winds about the carriage attendant, regret lingers a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit is gone beyond reach; no sage's count can follow—sorrow knots the carriage guard, regret stalls a hundred ways.

sentences.zh: 下官夙禀名節，恩義軫慕，望𡑞結哀，輒欲率荊、江、湘三州僚吏，建碑壟首，庶徽猷有述，茂則方存。

translations.literal: I have long received name and integrity, pity and righteousness tie my heart with admiration; facing his tomb I gather sorrow and wish at once to lead the officials of Jing, Jiang, and Xiang in raising a stele at the mound's head, so his good rule may be told and his flourishing virtue remain on record.
translations.idiomatic: I have long held to honor and owed him duty and love; before his mound my grief knots tight, and I would lead the officers of Jing, Jiang, and Xiang to raise a stele at the gravehead, so his fine rule may be told and his bright example stand.

sentences.zh: 昔子香淳德，留銘江介，鉅平遺烈，墮淚漢南，況道尊前往，惠積聯綿者哉。

translations.literal: In former days Zi Xiang's pure virtue left a memorial at the Jiang reaches; Ju Ping's surviving glory made men weep south of Han—how much more when the Way is exalted and kindness accumulates in long strands?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiang's pure conduct left its stone on the Yangtze; Yang Hu's legacy drew tears south of the Han—how much more when the Way stands high and kindness runs on without break?

sentences.zh: 下官今便反假，無由躬事刊斲，須至西州鳩集所資，託中書侍郎劉繪營辦。」

translations.literal: I shall return from leave at once and have no way to oversee the cutting myself; I must wait until I reach West Province to gather funds, and entrust Vice Director of the Secretariat Liu Hui to arrange it.」
translations.idiomatic: I go back on leave now and cannot cut the stone myself; I must reach West Province to gather what is needed and ask Vice Director Liu Hui of the Secretariat to see it done.」

sentences.zh: 藹又與右率沈約書曰：「夫道宣餘烈，竹帛有時先朽，德孚遺事，金石更非後亡。

translations.literal: Yue wrote again to Shen Yue, Right Commandant: 「The Way proclaims surviving glory—bamboo and silk may first rot; virtue wins over what is left—metal and stone are all the more not lost afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Le Yue wrote again to Shen Yue, right commandant: 「The Way outlives a man—bamboo and silk may fail first; virtue holds what remains—metal and stone are less likely to perish after.

sentences.zh: 丞相獨秀生民，傍照日月。

translations.literal: The Chancellor alone stands eminent among the living, shining beside sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor stood alone among men, lit like sun and moon beside them.

sentences.zh: 標勝丘園，素履穆於忠義，譽應華衮，功迹著於弼諧。

translations.literal: He marked victory in hill and garden; plain conduct was grave in loyalty and righteousness; fame answered the imperial robe; deeds of merit showed in aiding harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He surpassed the hills and gardens in renown; his plain walk was steeped in loyalty; praise met the imperial robe; his service showed in aiding the throne.

sentences.zh: 無得而稱，理絕照載。

translations.literal: None can name it fully; reason cuts off what illumination records.
translations.idiomatic: Words fail him; reason itself stops where light would write.

sentences.zh: 若夫日用闃寂，雖無取於錙銖，歲功宏達，諒有寄於衡石。

translations.literal: If daily use seems quiet and still, though it takes nothing from a hair's weight, the year's great achievement broadly attained surely has its rest in the balancer stone.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day he seemed still and without show, as if he weighed not a hair; yet the year's great work rested on him like stone on the scale.

sentences.zh: 竊承貴州士民，或建碑表，俾我荊南，閱感無地。

translations.literal: I hear privately that gentry and people of your noble province sometimes raise steles and tables—making our southern Jing feel nowhere to lodge its gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that in your noble province some gentry and common folk would raise steles—leaving our south Jing with no ground to set its thanks.

sentences.zh: 且作紀江、漢，道基分陝，衣冠禮樂，咸被後昆。

translations.literal: Moreover, at Ji on the Jiang and Han he laid the Way's foundation; at Fen and Shaan the ritual caps and music spread—all reached later generations.
translations.idiomatic: He set the Way's base on the Jiang and Han; at Fen and Shaan caps and rites spread—blessing reached sons and grandsons.

translations.idiomatic: the humble earth's surviving ways—perhaps his great flame will not go out.

sentences.zh: 荊、江、湘三州策名不少，竝欲各率毫釐，少申景慕。

translations.literal: Jing, Jiang, and Xiang have no few registered names who all wish to lead whatever trifle each may, to express a little of their admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, Jiang, and Xiang count many men on the rolls who would each give what little he can to show a measure of regard.

sentences.zh: 斯文之託，歷選惟疑，必待文蔚辭宗，德僉茂履，非高明而誰？

translations.literal: The entrusting of this text, choice after choice full of doubt, must await a literary cloud and phrase-master, virtue gathered and flourishing conduct—who if not the lofty and bright?
translations.idiomatic: To entrust this text is to choose and doubt again—it must wait on a master of letters, on gathered virtue and full conduct. Who if not one high and clear?

sentences.zh: 豈能騁無愧之辭，詶式瞻之望。

translations.literal: How could I gallop words without shame and answer the hope of those who gaze in reverence?
translations.idiomatic: How could I run forth shameless phrases and meet the hope of those who look up to him?

sentences.zh: 吾西州窮士，一介寂寥，恩周榮譽，澤遍衣食，永惟道廕，日月就遠，緬尋遺烈，觸目崩心。

translations.literal: I am a poor scholar of the western province, lonely and obscure of station; grace has ringed me in honor, bounty has reached through food and clothing; ever I recall his Way's shade as sun and moon draw away, and tracing his lingering glory, every sight shatters the heart.
translations.idiomatic: I am a poor man of the western province, obscure and alone; you have heaped honor on me and spread bounty through food and clothing. Ever I recall the shade of his Way as sun and moon recede; when I trace his lingering glory, every sight breaks my heart.

sentences.zh: 常謂福齊南山，慶鍾仁壽，吾儕小人，貽塵帷蓋。

translations.literal: I used always to say his blessing would match the southern mountains and his joy ring in kind longevity—we petty men merely trailing dust behind his canopy.
translations.idiomatic: I used to say his fortune would stand with the southern mountains and his joy ring in benevolent longevity—we petty men only trailing dust from his canopy.

sentences.zh: 豈圖一旦遂投此請。

translations.literal: Who thought that in a single day I would be hurled into this request.
translations.idiomatic: Who could have thought that in a single day I would be cast into this commission.

sentences.zh: 憗遺之感，朝野同悲。

translations.literal: The lingering grief at what was left behind—court and country mourn alike.
translations.idiomatic: Grief at what was left behind fills court and country alike.

sentences.zh: 承當刊石紀功，傳華千載，宜須盛述，實允來談。

translations.literal: I hear you are to cut stone and record his merit, to pass glory through a thousand years—a grand narration is precisely what your words invite.
translations.idiomatic: I hear you will cut stone and record his merit, that his fame may flower for a thousand years—a full account is exactly what your message asks.

sentences.zh: 郭有道漢末之匹夫，非蔡伯喈不足以偶三絕，謝安石素族之台輔，時無麗藻，迄乃有碑無文。

translations.literal: Guo Youdao was but a common man at the end of Han; without Cai Yong's brush the triple perfection could not be paired. Xie Anshi was a chief minister from a plain clan; with no fine stylus of the age, in the end there was a stele but no text.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Youdao was a nobody at the end of Han; without Cai Yong's brush the triple perfection could not be matched. Xie Anshi was a chief minister from an undistinguished house; with no fine writer at hand, in the end there was a stele but no inscription.

sentences.zh: 況文獻王冠冕彜倫，儀形㝢內，自非一世辭宗，難或與此。

translations.literal: How much more Prince Wenxian, crown of the ordinances within the four seas—unless some age's master of letters, scarcely anyone could meet this task.
translations.idiomatic: How much more Prince Wenxian, crown of ritual order within the four seas—unless a master of letters of the age, scarcely anyone could undertake this.

sentences.zh: 約閭閈鄙人，名不入第，歘酬今旨，便是以禮許人，聞命慙顏，已不覺汗之沾背也。

translations.literal: Yue is a low man from the lanes, his name not listed among equals; to answer this charge at once would be to grant the rites where one is unworthy—hearing the commission, my face burns with shame; I am already conscious of sweat soaking my back.
translations.idiomatic: Yue is a mean man from the lanes, his name not among the ranked; to answer this charge at once would be to accept rites beyond my worth—hearing the commission, shame floods my face and sweat soaks my back before I know it.

translations.idiomatic: Ziliang, courtesy name Jing'ai.

translations.literal: At first Ni had adopted the Marquis of Yufu Zixiang as heir; Ziliang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxin, a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At first Ni had adopted Zixiang, Marquis of Yufu, as heir; Ziliang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxin with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 子響還本，子廉為世子。

translations.literal: When Zixiang returned to his birth status, Ziliang became heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Zixiang reverted to his birth family, Ziliang became heir.

translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at caring for his younger brothers.

translations.literal: He died in the eleventh year; posthumously made palace attendant, posthumous title Lamented Heir.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year and was posthumously made palace attendant, with the posthumous title Lamented Heir.

sentences.zh: 第三子子操，泉陵侯。

translations.literal: The third son Zicao, Marquis of Quanling.
translations.idiomatic: The third son Zicao, Marquis of Quanling.

sentences.zh: 王侯出身官無定，准素姓三公長子一人為員外郎。

translations.literal: Princes and marquises had no fixed starting office; only plain-clan eldest sons of the Three Excellencies were made Supplemental Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: For princes and marquises there was no fixed entry office; only the eldest sons of plain-clan Three Excellencies were made supplemental gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 建武中，子操解褐為給事中，自此齊末皆以為例。

translations.literal: In Jianwu, Zicao began office as Palace Attendant; from then to the end of Qi this was the rule.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu, Zicao entered office as palace attendant; from then until the end of Qi this was the precedent.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，南康侯子恪為吳郡太守，避王敬則難奔歸，以子操為寧遠將軍、吳郡太守。

translations.literal: In Yongtai year 1, the Marquis of Nankang Zike was Administrator of Wu commandery; fleeing Wang Jingze's crisis he returned home, and Zicao was made General Pacifying the Distance and Administrator of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai year 1, Zike, Marquis of Nankang, was Administrator of Wu; fleeing Wang Jingze's uprising he came home, and Zicao was made General Pacifying the Distance and Administrator of Wu.

sentences.zh: 永元中，為黃門郎。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era he was Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongyuan era he was yellow gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 義師圍城，子操與弟宜陽侯子光卒於尚書都座。

translations.literal: When the righteous army besieged the capital, Zicao and his brother the Marquis of Yiyang Ziguang died in the Masters of Writing hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army besieged the capital, Zicao and his brother Ziguang, Marquis of Yiyang, died in the Masters of Writing hall.

sentences.zh: 第四子子行，洮陽侯，早卒。

translations.literal: The fourth son Zixing, Marquis of Taoyang, died young.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth son Zixing, Marquis of Taoyang, died young.

translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lin succeeded; when the present sovereign received the abdication, an edict said: 「To honor and exalt past generations is righteousness fixed in the eternal norms.

sentences.zh: 朕當此樂推，思弘前典。

translations.literal: As I face this joyful yielding of the throne, I think to enlarge the former canons.
translations.idiomatic: As I take this willing yielding of the throne, I mean to enlarge the former canons.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：楚元王高祖亞弟，無功漢世，東平憲王辭位永平，未及光武之業，梁孝惑於勝、詭，安平心隔晉運。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Prince Yuan of Chu was Emperor Gaozu's younger brother but won no merit in Han; the Exalted Prince of Dongping resigned his fief in Yongping and fell short of Emperor Guangwu's achievement; Prince Xiao of Liang was misled by Sheng and Gui; the Prince of Anping's heart turned from the Jin fate.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Prince Yuan of Chu was Emperor Gaozu's younger brother yet won no merit in Han; the Exalted Prince of Dongping resigned his fief in Yongping and never matched Guangwu's achievement; Prince Xiao of Liang was led astray by Sheng and Gui; the Prince of Anping's heart stood apart from the Jin mandate.

sentences.zh: 蕃輔貴盛，地實高危，持滿戒盈，鮮能全德。

translations.literal: As territorial supporters grow noble and great, their ground is truly perilous; holding fullness and guarding against excess—few keep their virtue whole.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier princes grow noble and great, their ground is truly perilous; to hold fullness and guard against excess—few keep virtue whole.

sentences.zh: 〔豫章〕宰相之器，誠有天真，因心無矯，率由遠度，故能光贊二祖，內和九族，實同周氏之初，周公以來，則未知所匹也。

translations.literal: [Prince of Yuzhang] had the makings of a chancellor in truth, innate and without forcing; following his far-reaching measure, he could therefore brighten and aid the two Founders, harmonize the nine kin within—truly like the Zhou at its founding; since the Duke of Zhou, none know his equal.
translations.idiomatic: [The Prince of Yuzhang] had the makings of a chancellor in truth, innate and without artifice; guided by far-reaching measure, he could brighten and aid the two Founders and harmonize the nine kin within—truly like the Zhou at its founding; since the Duke of Zhou, none know his equal.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：堂堂烈考，德邁前蹤。

translations.literal: In praise: Majestic and bright, our august father; his virtue surpasses the tracks of old.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Majestic and bright, our august father; his virtue outruns the tracks of old.

sentences.zh: 移忠以孝，植友惟恭。

translations.literal: He moved loyalty into filial piety, planted friendship in reverence alone.
translations.idiomatic: He moved loyalty into filial piety and planted friendship in reverence alone.

sentences.zh: 帝載初造，我王奮庸。

translations.literal: When the imperial burden was first wrought, our prince took up the work.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial charge was first laid, our prince took up the task.

sentences.zh: 邦家有闕，我王彌縫。

translations.literal: Where state and clan had gaps, our prince closed the seam.
translations.idiomatic: Where state and house had gaps, our prince closed the seam.

sentences.zh: 道深日用，事緝民雍。

translations.literal: His Way ran deep in daily use; his affairs wove the people's peace.
translations.idiomatic: His Way ran deep in daily use; his affairs wove the people into peace.

sentences.zh: 愛傳餘祀，聲流景鍾。

translations.literal: His love passes to remaining generations; his fame flows to the bell of brightest glory.
translations.idiomatic: His love passes to generations yet to come; his fame flows to the Bright Bell.
